   450→    def _try_tier0(
   451→        self, text: str, context_hash: str, start: float
   452→    ) -> Optional[RoutingResult]:
   453→        """Try Tier 0 regex parse."""
   454→        parse = self._parser.parse(text)
   455→        if not parse.matched or parse.confidence < self._config.tier0_confidence:
   456→            return None
   457→
   458→        # Execute if command_fn available
   459→        responses = []
   460→        if self._command_fn and parse.command:
   461→            try:
   462→                resp = self._command_fn(parse.command)
   463→                responses.append(resp)
   464→            except Exception as e:
   465→                responses.append(SynapseResponse(
   466→                    id=parse.command.id, success=False, error=str(e),
   467→                ))
   468→
   469→        result = RoutingResult(
   470→            success=True,
   471→            tier=RoutingTier.INSTANT,
   472→            answer=f"Parsed as {parse.pattern_name}",
   473→            commands=[parse.command] if parse.command else [],
   474→            responses=responses,
   475→            confidence=parse.confidence,
   476→            latency_ms=(time.monotonic() - start) * 1000,
   477→            metadata={
   478→                "pattern": parse.pattern_name,
   479→                "extracted": parse.extracted,
   480→            },
   481→        )
   482→
   483→        self._cache_result("instant", text, context_hash, result)
   484→        self._pin_tier(text, context_hash, RoutingTier.INSTANT.value,
   485→                       pin_key=f"{text.strip().lower()}|{context_hash}")
   486→        self._record_metric(RoutingTier.INSTANT, result.latency_ms)
   487→        return result

   489→    def _try_tier1(
   490→        self,
   491→        lookup: KnowledgeLookupResult,
   492→        text: str,
   493→        context_hash: str,
   494→        start: float,
   495→    ) -> Optional[RoutingResult]:
   496→        """Try Tier 1 knowledge lookup (uses pre-computed result)."""
   497→        if not lookup.found or lookup.confidence < self._config.tier1_confidence:
   498→            return None
   499→
   500→        result = RoutingResult(
   501→            success=True,
   502→            tier=RoutingTier.FAST,
   503→            answer=lookup.answer,
   504→            confidence=lookup.confidence,
   505→            latency_ms=(time.monotonic() - start) * 1000,
   506→            metadata={
   507→                "topic": lookup.topic,
   508→                "sources": lookup.sources,
   509→                "agent_hint": lookup.agent_hint,
   510→            },
   511→        )
   512→
   513→        self._cache_result("fast", text, context_hash, result)
   514→        self._pin_tier(text, context_hash, RoutingTier.FAST.value,
   515→                       pin_key=f"{text.strip().lower()}|{context_hash}")
   516→        self._record_metric(RoutingTier.FAST, result.latency_ms)

   519→    def _pin_tier(self, input_text: str, context_hash: str, tier_value: str,
   520→                  pin_key: Optional[str] = None):
   521→        """Record a tier pin for future consistency."""
   522→        if pin_key is None:
   523→            pin_key = f"{input_text.strip().lower()}|{context_hash}"
   524→        with self._tier_pins_lock.write_lock():
   525→            # LRU eviction: remove oldest 10% when at capacity
   526→            if len(self._tier_pins) >= _MAX_TIER_PINS and pin_key not in self._tier_pins:
   527→                evict_count = max(1, len(self._tier_pins) // 10)
   528→                for old_key in list(self._tier_pins.keys())[:evict_count]:
   529→                    del self._tier_pins[old_key]
   530→            self._tier_pins[pin_key] = tier_value
   531→
   532→    def _try_pinned_tier(
   533→        self,
   534→        tier_value: str,
   535→        text: str,
   536→        context: Dict,
   537→        context_hash: str,
   538→        start: float,
   539→    ) -> Optional[RoutingResult]:
   540→        """Re-execute the pinned tier directly."""
   541→        if tier_value == RoutingTier.RECIPE.value and self._config.enable_recipes:
   542→            return self._try_recipe(text, context_hash, start)
   543→        if tier_value == RoutingTier.INSTANT.value and self._config.enable_tier0:
   544→            return self._try_tier0(text, context_hash, start)
   545→        if tier_value == RoutingTier.FAST.value and self._config.enable_tier1:
   546→            hint = self._knowledge.lookup(text)
   547→            if hint:
   548→                return self._try_tier1(hint, text, context_hash, start)
   549→        if tier_value == RoutingTier.STANDARD.value and self._config.enable_tier2:
   550→            hint = self._knowledge.lookup(text)
   551→            return self._try_tier2(text, context, context_hash, start, hint)
   552→        if tier_value == RoutingTier.DEEP.value and self._config.enable_tier3:
   553→            hint = self._knowledge.lookup(text)
   554→            return self._try_tier3(text, context, context_hash, start, hint)
   555→        return None

   557→    def _try_tier2(
   558→        self,
   559→        text: str,
   560→        context: Dict,
   561→        context_hash: str,
   562→        start: float,
   563→        tier1_hint: Optional[KnowledgeLookupResult] = None,
   564→    ) -> Optional[RoutingResult]:
   565→        """Try Tier 2: Haiku LLM with fixed system prompt."""
   566→        try:
   567→            client = self._get_llm_client()
   568→            if client is None:
   569→                return None
   570→
   571→            # Build enriched user message via context_enrichment module
   572→            user_message = enrich_context(
   573→                message=text,
   574→                tier1_hint=tier1_hint,
   575→                memory=self._memory,
   576→            )
   577→
   578→            response = client.messages.create(
   579→                model=self._config.llm_model_fast,
   580→                max_tokens=1024,
   581→                system=_TIER2_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
   582→                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_message}],
   583→            )
   584→
   585→            # Parse structured response
   586→            raw_text = response.content[0].text
   587→            parsed = self._parse_llm_response(raw_text)
   588→
   589→            commands = []
   590→            responses = []
   591→            answer = parsed.get("answer", raw_text)
   592→
   593→            if parsed.get("action") == "command" and parsed.get("command_type"):
   594→                cmd = SynapseCommand(
   595→                    type=parsed["command_type"],
   596→                    id=deterministic_uuid(
   597→                        f"tier2:{parsed['command_type']}:{json.dumps(parsed.get('payload', {}), sort_keys=True)}",
   598→                        "cmd",
   599→                    ),
   600→                    payload=parsed.get("payload", {}),
   601→                )
   602→                commands.append(cmd)
   603→                if self._command_fn:
   604→                    try:
   605→                        resp = self._command_fn(cmd)
   606→                        responses.append(resp)
   607→                    except Exception as e:
   608→                        responses.append(SynapseResponse(
   609→                            id=cmd.id, success=False, error=str(e),
   610→                        ))
   611→
   612→            tier2_meta = {
   613→                "model": self._config.llm_model_fast,
   614→                "reasoning": parsed.get("reasoning", ""),
   615→                "action": parsed.get("action", "answer"),
   616→            }
   617→            if tier1_hint and tier1_hint.found:
   618→                tier2_meta["tier1_enrichment"] = {
   619→                    "topic": tier1_hint.topic,
   620→                    "confidence": tier1_hint.confidence,
   621→                    "sources": tier1_hint.sources,
   622→                }
   623→
   624→            result = RoutingResult(
   625→                success=True,
   626→                tier=RoutingTier.STANDARD,
   627→                answer=answer,
   628→                commands=commands,
   629→                responses=responses,
   630→                confidence=parsed.get("confidence", 0.7),
   631→                latency_ms=(time.monotonic() - start) * 1000,
   632→                metadata=tier2_meta,
   633→            )
   634→
   635→            self._cache_result("standard", text, context_hash, result)
   636→            self._pin_tier(text, context_hash, RoutingTier.STANDARD.value,
   637→                           pin_key=f"{text.strip().lower()}|{context_hash}")
   638→            self._record_metric(RoutingTier.STANDARD, result.latency_ms)
   639→            return result
   640→
   641→        except Exception as e:
   642→            logger.warning("Tier 2 failed: %s", e)
   643→            return None

   645→    def _try_tier3(
   646→        self,
   647→        text: str,
   648→        context: Dict,
   649→        context_hash: str,
   650→        start: float,
   651→        tier1_hint: Optional[KnowledgeLookupResult] = None,
   652→    ) -> Optional[RoutingResult]:
   653→        """Try Tier 3: Full agent loop (async or sync)."""
   654→        handle = deterministic_uuid(f"tier3:{text}:{context_hash}", "handle")
   655→
   656→        if self._config.tier3_async:
   657→            # Launch in background thread
   658→            thread = threading.Thread(
   659→                target=self._tier3_worker,
   660→                args=(handle, text, context, context_hash, tier1_hint),
   661→                daemon=True,
   662→            )
   663→            thread.start()
   664→
   665→            result = RoutingResult(
   666→                success=True,
   667→                tier=RoutingTier.DEEP,
   668→                answer="Processing in background...",
   669→                confidence=0.5,
   670→                latency_ms=(time.monotonic() - start) * 1000,
   671→                async_handle=handle,
   672→                metadata={"async": True},
   673→            )
   674→            self._record_metric(RoutingTier.DEEP, result.latency_ms)
   675→            return result
   676→        else:
   677→            # Synchronous execution
   678→            return self._tier3_sync(text, context, context_hash, start, tier1_hint)

   680→    def _tier3_worker(
   681→        self,
   682→        handle: str,
   683→        text: str,
   684→        context: Dict,
   685→        context_hash: str,
   686→        tier1_hint: Optional[KnowledgeLookupResult] = None,
   687→    ):
   688→        """Background worker for Tier 3 agent execution."""
   689→        start = time.monotonic()
   690→        try:
   691→            result = self._tier3_sync(text, context, context_hash, start, tier1_hint)
   692→            if result:
   693→                with self._async_lock:
   694→                    self._async_results[handle] = result
   695→        except Exception as e:
   696→            logger.error("Tier 3 worker failed: %s", e)
   697→            with self._async_lock:
   698→                self._async_results[handle] = RoutingResult(
   699→                    success=False,
   700→                    tier=RoutingTier.DEEP,
   701→                    answer=f"Agent execution failed: {e}",
   702→                    latency_ms=(time.monotonic() - start) * 1000,
   703→                )

   705→    def _tier3_sync(
   706→        self,
   707→        text: str,
   708→        context: Dict,
   709→        context_hash: str,
   710→        start: float,
   711→        tier1_hint: Optional[KnowledgeLookupResult] = None,
   712→    ) -> Optional[RoutingResult]:
   713→        """Synchronous Tier 3 agent execution."""
   714→        try:
   715→            client = self._get_llm_client()
   716→            if client is None:
   717→                return None
   718→
   719→            # Build enriched user message via context_enrichment module
   720→            user_message = enrich_context(
   721→                message=text,
   722→                tier1_hint=tier1_hint,
   723→            )
   724→
   725→            # Use deeper model for planning
   726→            response = client.messages.create(
   727→                model=self._config.llm_model_deep,
   728→                max_tokens=4096,
   729→                system=_TIER2_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
   730→                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_message}],
   731→            )
   732→
   733→            raw_text = response.content[0].text
   734→            parsed = self._parse_llm_response(raw_text)
   735→
   736→            result = RoutingResult(
   737→                success=True,
   738→                tier=RoutingTier.DEEP,
   739→                answer=parsed.get("answer", raw_text),
   740→                confidence=parsed.get("confidence", 0.6),
   741→                latency_ms=(time.monotonic() - start) * 1000,
   742→                metadata={
   743→                    "model": self._config.llm_model_deep,
   744→                    "reasoning": parsed.get("reasoning", ""),
   745→                },
   746→            )
   747→
   748→            self._cache_result("deep", text, context_hash, result)
   749→            self._pin_tier(text, context_hash, RoutingTier.DEEP.value,
   750→                           pin_key=f"{text.strip().lower()}|{context_hash}")
   751→            self._record_metric(RoutingTier.DEEP, result.latency_ms)
   752→            return result
   753→
   754→        except Exception as e:
   755→            logger.warning("Tier 3 sync failed: %s", e)
   756→            return None
   757→
   758→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   759→    # Async result retrieval
   760→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   761→
   762→    def get_async_result(self, handle: str) -> Optional[RoutingResult]:
   763→        """
   764→        Poll for async Tier 3 result.
   765→
   766→        Returns None if still processing, RoutingResult when done.
   767→        """
   768→        with self._async_lock:
   769→            return self._async_results.pop(handle, None)
   770→
   771→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   772→    # LLM client
   773→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   774→
   775→    def _get_llm_client(self):
   776→        """Lazy-initialize Anthropic client."""
   777→        if self._llm_client is not None:
   778→            return self._llm_client
   779→
   780→        if not self._config.llm_api_key:
   781→            return None
   782→
   783→        try:
   784→            import anthropic
   785→            self._llm_client = anthropic.Anthropic(
   786→                api_key=self._config.llm_api_key,
   787→            )
   788→            return self._llm_client
   789→        except ImportError:
   790→            logger.warning("anthropic package not installed — Tier 2/3 disabled")
   791→            return None
   792→
   793→    def _parse_llm_response(self, text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   794→        """Parse structured JSON from LLM response."""
   795→        # Try to extract JSON from markdown code blocks
   796→        if "```" in text:
   797→            parts = text.split("```")
   798→            for part in parts:
   799→                part = part.strip()
   800→                if part.startswith("json"):
   801→                    part = part[4:].strip()
   802→                try:
   803→                    return json.loads(part)
   804→                except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
   805→                    continue
   806→
   807→        # Try direct JSON parse
   808→        try:
   809→            return json.loads(text)
   810→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
   811→            pass
   812→
   813→        # Fallback: treat as plain text answer
   814→        return {"action": "answer", "answer": text, "confidence": 0.6}
   815→
   816→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   817→    # Caching helpers
   818→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   819→
   820→    def _cache_result(
   821→        self, tier: str, text: str, context_hash: str, result: RoutingResult
   822→    ):
   823→        """Store result in cache if enabled."""
   824→        if self._config.enable_cache:
   825→            self._cache.put(tier, text, context_hash, result)
   826→
   827→    def _hash_context(self, context: Dict) -> str:
   828→        """Hash context dict for cache keying.
   829→
   830→        Uses xxhash (~100x faster than SHA-256) when available.
   831→        """
   832→        if not context:
   833→            return ""
   834→        try:
   835→            import orjson
   836→            raw = orjson.dumps(context, option=orjson.OPT_SORT_KEYS, default=str)
   837→        except (ImportError, TypeError):
   838→            raw = json.dumps(context, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()
   839→        try:
   840→            import xxhash
   841→            return xxhash.xxh64(raw).hexdigest()[:16]
   842→        except ImportError:
   843→            return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()[:16]
   844→
   845→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   846→    # Metrics
   847→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   848→
   849→    def _record_metric(self, tier: RoutingTier, latency_ms: float, success: bool = True):
   850→        """Record routing metric and epoch outcome."""
   851→        self._tier_counts[tier.value] = self._tier_counts.get(tier.value, 0) + 1
   852→        if tier.value not in self._tier_latencies:
   853→            self._tier_latencies[tier.value] = collections.deque(maxlen=1000)
   854→        self._tier_latencies[tier.value].append(latency_ms)
   855→        self._total_routes += 1
   856→
   857→        # Feed epoch adapter for adaptive threshold adjustment
   858→        self._epoch.record(tier.value, success, latency_ms)
   859→
   860→    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   861→        """Return routing statistics."""
   862→        tier_stats = {}
   863→        for tier_name in sorted(self._tier_counts):  # sorted: He2025
   864→            count = self._tier_counts[tier_name]
   865→            latencies = self._tier_latencies.get(tier_name, [])
   866→            tier_stats[tier_name] = {
   867→                "count": count,
   868→                "avg_ms": round_float(kahan_sum(latencies) / len(latencies)) if latencies else 0,
   869→                "max_ms": round_float(max(latencies)) if latencies else 0,
   870→            }
   871→
   872→        return {
   873→            "total_routes": self._total_routes,
   874→            "tiers": tier_stats,
   875→            "cache": self._cache.stats(),
   876→            "knowledge": self._knowledge.stats(),
   877→            "epoch": self._epoch.stats(),
   878→        }
   879→
   880→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   881→    # Drop-in compatibility
   882→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   883→
   884→    def as_command_fn(self) -> Callable[[SynapseCommand], SynapseResponse]:
   885→        """
   886→        Return a command_fn-compatible wrapper.
   887→
   888→        Allows the router to be used anywhere command_fn is expected.
   889→        The command's payload must include a 'text' field for routing.
   890→        """
   891→        def wrapper(cmd: SynapseCommand) -> SynapseResponse:
   892→            text = cmd.payload.get("text", cmd.payload.get("query", ""))
   893→            if not text:
   894→                return SynapseResponse(
   895→                    id=cmd.id,
   896→                    success=False,
   897→                    error="No 'text' or 'query' field in payload",
   898→                )
   899→
   900→            result = self.route(text, context=cmd.payload.get("context"))
   901→            return SynapseResponse(
   902→                id=cmd.id,
   903→                success=result.success,
   904→                data={
   905→                    "answer": result.answer,
   906→                    "tier": result.tier.value,
   907→                    "confidence": result.confidence,
   908→                    "latency_ms": result.latency_ms,
   909→                    "cached": result.cached,
   910→                    "async_handle": result.async_handle,
   911→                },
   912→            )
   913→
   914→        return wrapper
   915→
   916→    @property
   917→    def parser(self) -> CommandParser:
   918→        """Access the Tier 0 parser."""
   919→        return self._parser
   920→
   921→    @property
   922→    def knowledge(self) -> KnowledgeIndex:
   923→        """Access the Tier 1 knowledge index."""
   924→        return self._knowledge
   925→
   926→    @property
   927→    def recipe_registry(self) -> RecipeRegistry:
   928→        """Access the recipe registry."""
   929→        return self._recipes
   930→
   931→    @property
   932→    def cache(self) -> ResponseCache:
   933→        """Access the response cache."""
   934→        return self._cache

1→"""
     2→Synapse Response Cache (He2025)
     3→
     4→Deterministic response caching via SHA-256 canonicalization.
     5→Same canonical input → same cached output → O(1) retrieval.
     6→
     7→Inspired by [He2025]: batch-invariant kernels + temperature 0 = identical
     8→output for identical input. Canonicalization enables cross-session caching.
     9→
    10→TTL strategy per tier:
    11→  Tier 1: 1h  (knowledge is static within session)
    12→  Tier 2: 30m (LLM responses may vary with context)
    13→  Tier 3: 10m (plans depend on mutable scene state)
    14→"""
    15→
    16→import hashlib
    17→import time
    18→import threading
    19→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    20→from typing import Dict, Optional, Any, Tuple
    21→
    22→# xxhash is ~100x faster than SHA-256 for cache keying (non-crypto use)
    23→try:
    24→    import xxhash
    25→    _XXHASH_AVAILABLE = True
    26→except ImportError:
    27→    _XXHASH_AVAILABLE = False
    28→
    29→
    30→def _fast_hash(data: str) -> str:
    31→    """Fast non-cryptographic hash for cache keys.
    32→
    33→    Uses xxhash (O(n) with tiny constant) when available,
    34→    falls back to SHA-256.
    35→    """
    36→    encoded = data.encode("utf-8")
    37→    if _XXHASH_AVAILABLE:
    38→        return xxhash.xxh64(encoded).hexdigest()
    39→    return hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()
    40→
    41→
    42→# Default TTLs per tier name
    43→_DEFAULT_TTLS: Dict[str, int] = {
    44→    "recipe": 0,    # No cache — already instant
    45→    "instant": 0,   # No cache — already instant
    46→    "fast": 3600,   # 1 hour
    47→    "standard": 1800,  # 30 minutes
    48→    "deep": 600,    # 10 minutes
    49→}
    50→
    51→
    52→@dataclass
    53→class _CacheEntry:
    54→    """Internal cache entry with expiry tracking."""
    55→    result: Any
    56→    created_at: float
    57→    ttl: int
    58→    tier: str
    59→    hits: int = 0
    60→
    61→    @property
    62→    def expired(self) -> bool:
    63→        if self.ttl <= 0:
    64→            return True  # TTL 0 = never cache
    65→        return (time.monotonic() - self.created_at) > self.ttl
    66→
    67→
    68→class ResponseCache:
    69→    """
    70→    Deterministic response cache using SHA-256 canonicalization.
    71→
    72→    Thread-safe via lock. LRU eviction when max_size exceeded.
    73→    """
    74→
    75→    def __init__(self, max_size: int = 500, ttl_seconds: int = 3600):
    76→        self._max_size = max_size
    77→        self._default_ttl = ttl_seconds
    78→        self._cache: Dict[str, _CacheEntry] = {}
    79→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
    80→        self._total_hits = 0
    81→        self._total_misses = 0
    82→        self._evictions = 0
    83→
    84→    def get(
    85→        self,
    86→        tier: str,
    87→        input_text: str,
    88→        context_hash: str = "",
    89→    ) -> Optional[Any]:
    90→        """
    91→        Look up cached result for canonical input.
    92→
    93→        Returns the cached RoutingResult or None on miss/expiry.
    94→        """
    95→        key = self._canonical_key(tier, input_text, context_hash)
    96→        with self._lock:
    97→            entry = self._cache.get(key)
    98→            if entry is None:
    99→                self._total_misses += 1
   100→                return None
   101→            if entry.expired:
   102→                del self._cache[key]
   103→                self._total_misses += 1
   104→                return None
   105→            entry.hits += 1
   106→            self._total_hits += 1
   107→            return entry.result
   108→
   109→    def put(
   110→        self,
   111→        tier: str,
   112→        input_text: str,
   113→        context_hash: str,
   114→        result: Any,
   115→        ttl: Optional[int] = None,
   116→    ):
   117→        """
   118→        Cache a result for the canonical input.
   119→
   120→        Uses tier-specific TTL if not provided.
   121→        """
   122→        if ttl is None:
   123→            ttl = _DEFAULT_TTLS.get(tier, self._default_ttl)
   124→        if ttl <= 0:
   125→            return  # Don't cache instant tiers
   126→
   127→        key = self._canonical_key(tier, input_text, context_hash)
   128→        with self._lock:
   129→            # Evict if at capacity
   130→            if len(self._cache) >= self._max_size and key not in self._cache:
   131→                self._evict_one()
   132→
   133→            self._cache[key] = _CacheEntry(
   134→                result=result,
   135→                created_at=time.monotonic(),
   136→                ttl=ttl,
   137→                tier=tier,
   138→            )
   139→
   140→    def invalidate(self, pattern: Optional[str] = None):
   141→        """
   142→        Clear cache entries.
   143→
   144→        Args:
   145→            pattern: If provided, only clear entries whose key contains pattern.
   146→                     If None, clear all entries.
   147→        """
   148→        with self._lock:
   149→            if pattern is None:
   150→                self._cache.clear()
   151→            else:
   152→                pattern_lower = pattern.lower()
   153→                keys_to_remove = [
   154→                    k for k in self._cache
   155→                    if pattern_lower in k.lower()
   156→                ]
   157→                for k in keys_to_remove:
   158→                    del self._cache[k]
   159→
   160→    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   161→        """Return cache statistics."""
   162→        with self._lock:
   163→            total = self._total_hits + self._total_misses
   164→            return {
   165→                "size": len(self._cache),
   166→                "max_size": self._max_size,
   167→                "hits": self._total_hits,
   168→                "misses": self._total_misses,
   169→                "hit_rate": (self._total_hits / total) if total > 0 else 0.0,
   170→                "evictions": self._evictions,
   171→            }
   172→
   173→    def _canonical_key(self, tier: str, input_text: str, context_hash: str) -> str:
   174→        """
   175→        Produce canonical cache key via SHA-256.
   176→
   177→        Canonicalization (He2025-inspired):
   178→        1. Strip whitespace, lowercase
   179→        2. Hash: SHA-256(tier + ":" + canonical_text + ":" + context_hash)
   180→        """
   181→        canonical = input_text.strip().lower()
   182→        raw = f"{tier}:{canonical}:{context_hash}"
   183→        return _fast_hash(raw)
   184→
   185→    def _evict_one(self):
   186→        """Batch eviction: remove expired entries, then oldest 10% by created_at.
   187→
   188→        Amortizes the O(n) scan cost by evicting multiple entries at once
   189→        instead of finding a single min on every put().
   190→        """
   191→        if not self._cache:
   192→            return
   193→
   194→        # Phase 1: sweep all expired entries
   195→        expired_keys = [k for k, e in self._cache.items() if e.expired]
   196→        if expired_keys:
   197→            for k in expired_keys:
   198→                del self._cache[k]
   199→            self._evictions += len(expired_keys)
   200→            return
   201→
   202→        # Phase 2: evict oldest 10% (minimum 1) sorted by created_at
   203→        batch_size = max(1, len(self._cache) // 10)
   204→        victims = sorted(
   205→            self._cache,
   206→            key=lambda k: self._cache[k].created_at,
   207→        )[:batch_size]
   208→        for k in victims:
   209→            del self._cache[k]
   210→        self._evictions += len(victims)
   211→

1→"""
     2→Synapse Tier 1: Knowledge Index
     3→
     4→In-memory knowledge lookup from RAG metadata, reference files, and memory.
     5→No LLM. Runs in <500ms.
     6→
     7→Degrades gracefully:
     8→  - With RAG + memory: full coverage
     9→  - With RAG only: no memory search fallback
    10→  - With memory only: no topic/reference lookup
    11→  - With neither: returns not-found (escalates to Tier 2)
    12→"""
    13→
    14→import json
    15→import os
    16→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    17→from pathlib import Path
    18→from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
    19→
    20→
    21→@dataclass
    22→class KnowledgeLookupResult:
    23→    """Result of Tier 1 knowledge lookup."""
    24→    found: bool
    25→    answer: str = ""
    26→    sources: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    27→    confidence: float = 0.0
    28→    topic: str = ""
    29→    agent_hint: str = ""
    30→    summary: str = ""
    31→    reference_file: str = ""
    32→
    33→
    34→class KnowledgeIndex:
    35→    """
    36→    Tier 1 knowledge lookup engine.
    37→
    38→    Loads RAG semantic index + reference files at init time.
    39→    Provides fast in-memory lookup without LLM calls.
    40→    """
    41→
    42→    def __init__(
    43→        self,
    44→        rag_root: Optional[str] = None,
    45→        memory: Optional[Any] = None,  # SynapseMemory
    46→    ):
    47→        """
    48→        Args:
    49→            rag_root: Path to RAG system root directory.
    50→            memory: Optional SynapseMemory instance for fallback search.
    51→        """
    52→        self._memory = memory
    53→        self._rag_root = Path(rag_root) if rag_root else None
    54→
    55→        # Data stores
    56→        self._semantic_index: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    57→        self._keyword_to_topics: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
    58→        self._reference_files: Dict[str, str] = {}
    59→        self._agent_relevance: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    60→        # Pre-indexed section headers: word -> [(file_stem, line_index, lines)]
    61→        self._section_index: Dict[str, List[tuple]] = {}
    62→
    63→        if self._rag_root:
    64→            self._load_semantic_index()
    65→            self._load_reference_files()
    66→            self._load_agent_relevance()
    67→
    68→    def _load_semantic_index(self):
    69→        """Load semantic_index.json and build inverted keyword index.
    70→
    71→        Supports two schema formats:
    72→          - SYNAPSE flat: {"topic": {"summary": ..., "keywords": [...]}}
    73→          - HOUDINI21_RAG nested: {"semantic_index": {"topics": {"topic": {...}}}}
    74→        Nested format is auto-detected and normalized to flat.
    75→        """
    76→        assert self._rag_root is not None
    77→        index_path = self._rag_root / "documentation" / "_metadata" / "semantic_index.json"
    78→        if not index_path.exists():
    79→            return
    80→
    81→        try:
    82→            with open(index_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    83→                raw = json.load(f)
    84→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
    85→            return
    86→
    87→        # Schema adapter: detect nested format and normalize
    88→        self._semantic_index = self._normalize_semantic_index(raw)
    89→
    90→        # Build inverted keyword index: word → [topic_names]
    91→        for topic_name, topic_data in sorted(self._semantic_index.items()):
    92→            keywords = []
    93→            if isinstance(topic_data, dict):
    94→                keywords = topic_data.get("keywords", [])
    95→                # Also index the topic name itself
    96→                keywords = list(keywords) + topic_name.lower().replace("_", " ").split()
    97→            for kw in keywords:
    98→                kw_lower = kw.lower()
    99→                if kw_lower not in self._keyword_to_topics:
   100→                    self._keyword_to_topics[kw_lower] = []
   101→                if topic_name not in self._keyword_to_topics[kw_lower]:
   102→                    self._keyword_to_topics[kw_lower].append(topic_name)
   103→
   104→        # Pre-compute IDF values (avoids per-query division)
   105→        self._keyword_idf: Dict[str, float] = {
   106→            word: 1.0 / len(topics) if topics else 0.0
   107→            for word, topics in self._keyword_to_topics.items()
   108→        }
   109→
   110→    @staticmethod
   111→    def _normalize_semantic_index(raw: dict) -> dict:
   112→        """Normalize nested RAG schema to flat SYNAPSE format.
   113→
   114→        Nested format (HOUDINI21_RAG):
   115→            {"semantic_index": {"topics": {"topic_name": {"primary_doc": ..., ...}}}}
   116→
   117→        Flat format (SYNAPSE):
   118→            {"topic_name": {"summary": ..., "keywords": [...]}}
   119→
   120→        If already flat, returns as-is.
   121→        """
   122→        # Detect nested format: has "semantic_index" key with "topics" inside
   123→        if "semantic_index" in raw and isinstance(raw.get("semantic_index"), dict):
   124→            nested = raw["semantic_index"]
   125→            topics = nested.get("topics", {})
   126→            if isinstance(topics, dict):
   127→                flat: Dict[str, Any] = {}
   128→                for topic_name, topic_data in sorted(topics.items()):
   129→                    if not isinstance(topic_data, dict):
   130→                        continue
   131→                    entry: Dict[str, Any] = {}
   132→                    # Map nested fields to flat equivalents
   133→                    if "primary_doc" in topic_data:
   134→                        entry["summary"] = topic_data["primary_doc"]
   135→                    if "description" in topic_data:
   136→                        entry["description"] = topic_data["description"]
   137→                    elif "primary_doc" in topic_data:
   138→                        entry["description"] = topic_data["primary_doc"]
   139→                    if "keywords" in topic_data:
   140→                        entry["keywords"] = topic_data["keywords"]
   141→                    if "reference_file" in topic_data:
   142→                        entry["reference_file"] = topic_data["reference_file"]
   143→                    # Preserve common_queries for test fixtures
   144→                    if "common_queries" in topic_data:
   145→                        entry["common_queries"] = topic_data["common_queries"]
   146→                    flat[topic_name] = entry
   147→                return flat
   148→
   149→        # Already flat format (or unrecognized) — return as-is
   150→        return raw
   151→
   152→    def _load_reference_files(self):
   153→        """Load .md reference files from skills directory and pre-index headers."""
   154→        if not self._rag_root:
   155→            return
   156→        ref_dir = self._rag_root / "skills" / "houdini21-reference"
   157→        if not ref_dir.exists():
   158→            return
   159→
   160→        for md_file in ref_dir.glob("*.md"):
   161→            try:
   162→                content = md_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   163→                self._reference_files[md_file.stem] = content
   164→            except OSError:
   165→                continue
   166→
   167→        # Pre-index section headers for O(1) word lookup
   168→        for file_stem, content in self._reference_files.items():
   169→            lines = content.split("\n")
   170→            for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   171→                if not line.startswith("#"):
   172→                    continue
   173→                header_words = set(line.lstrip("#").strip().lower().split())
   174→                for word in header_words:
   175→                    if word not in self._section_index:
   176→                        self._section_index[word] = []
   177→                    self._section_index[word].append((file_stem, i, lines))
   178→
   179→    def _load_agent_relevance(self):
   180→        """Load agent_relevance_map.json if available."""
   181→        if not self._rag_root:
   182→            return
   183→        rel_path = self._rag_root / "documentation" / "_metadata" / "agent_relevance_map.json"
   184→        if not rel_path.exists():
   185→            return
   186→        try:
   187→            with open(rel_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   188→                self._agent_relevance = json.load(f)
   189→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
   190→            pass
   191→
   192→    def lookup(self, query: str) -> KnowledgeLookupResult:
   193→        """
   194→        Look up knowledge for a query.
   195→
   196→        Strategy (first match wins):
   197→        1. Keyword match against inverted index → topic → answer
   198→        2. Section header match in reference files
   199→        3. Memory search fallback
   200→        4. Not found (escalate)
   201→        """
   202→        if not query or not query.strip():
   203→            return KnowledgeLookupResult(found=False)
   204→
   205→        query_lower = query.lower().strip()
   206→        query_words = set(self._tokenize(query_lower))
   207→
   208→        # Strategy 1: Keyword index match
   209→        result = self._match_keywords(query_words)
   210→        if result:
   211→            return result
   212→
   213→        # Strategy 2: Reference file section match
   214→        result = self._match_reference_sections(query_lower, query_words)
   215→        if result:
   216→            return result
   217→
   218→        # Strategy 3: VEX symptom diagnosis (natural-language)
   219→        result = self._match_vex_symptoms(query_lower)
   220→        if result:
   221→            return result
   222→
   223→        # Strategy 4: Memory fallback
   224→        result = self._match_memory(query)
   225→        if result:
   226→            return result
   227→
   228→        return KnowledgeLookupResult(found=False)
   229→
   230→    # Module-level constant — avoids re-allocating on every call
   231→    _STOPWORDS = frozenset({
   232→        "what", "is", "the", "a", "an", "how", "do", "i", "to", "in",
   233→        "on", "of", "for", "can", "you", "me", "my", "this", "that",
   234→        "with", "from", "about", "does", "it", "get", "show",
   235→    })
   236→
   237→    def _tokenize(self, text: str) -> List[str]:
   238→        """Extract meaningful words from text."""
   239→        words = []
   240→        for word in text.split():
   241→            cleaned = word.strip("?!.,;:'\"")
   242→            if cleaned and cleaned not in self._STOPWORDS and len(cleaned) > 1:
   243→                words.append(cleaned)
   244→        return words
   245→
   246→    def _match_keywords(self, query_words: set) -> Optional[KnowledgeLookupResult]:
   247→        """Match query words against inverted keyword index."""
   248→        if not self._keyword_to_topics:
   249→            return None
   250→
   251→        # Score topics by keyword overlap with IDF tiebreaker
   252→        # Each match contributes 1.0 (count) + IDF bonus (rare keywords score higher)
   253→        # Count remains the primary signal; IDF disambiguates equal-count ties
   254→        topic_scores: Dict[str, float] = {}
   255→        for word in query_words:
   256→            matching_topics = self._keyword_to_topics.get(word, [])
   257→            idf = self._keyword_idf.get(word, 0.0)
   258→            for topic in matching_topics:
   259→                topic_scores[topic] = topic_scores.get(topic, 0.0) + 1.0 + idf
   260→
   261→        if not topic_scores:
   262→            return None
   263→
   264→        # Best topic by overlap count
   265→        best_topic = max(topic_scores, key=lambda k: topic_scores[k])
   266→        best_score = topic_scores[best_topic]
   267→
   268→        # Require at least 1 keyword match; confidence scales with overlap
   269→        if best_score < 1:
   270→            return None
   271→
   272→        confidence = min(0.9, 0.4 + 0.15 * best_score)
   273→        topic_data = self._semantic_index.get(best_topic, {})
   274→
   275→        # Build answer from topic metadata
   276→        answer_parts = []
   277→        if isinstance(topic_data, dict):
   278→            if "summary" in topic_data:
   279→                answer_parts.append(topic_data["summary"])
   280→            if "description" in topic_data:
   281→                answer_parts.append(topic_data["description"])
   282→
   283→            # Enrich with reference file content if topic maps to one
   284→            ref_key = topic_data.get("reference_file", best_topic)
   285→            if ref_key in self._reference_files:
   286→                # Include first section (up to 500 chars)
   287→                ref_content = self._reference_files[ref_key][:500]
   288→                answer_parts.append(f"\n---\nReference:\n{ref_content}")
   289→
   290→        answer = "\n".join(answer_parts) if answer_parts else f"Topic: {best_topic}"
   291→
   292→        # Get agent hint from relevance map
   293→        agent_hint = ""
   294→        if isinstance(self._agent_relevance, dict):
   295→            agent_hint = self._agent_relevance.get(best_topic, "")
   296→
   297→        sources = [f"semantic_index:{best_topic}"]
   298→
   299→        # Extract discrete metadata for structured response
   300→        summary = ""
   301→        ref_file = ""
   302→        if isinstance(topic_data, dict):
   303→            summary = topic_data.get("summary", "")
   304→            ref_file = topic_data.get("reference_file", "")
   305→
   306→        return KnowledgeLookupResult(
   307→            found=True,
   308→            answer=answer,
   309→            sources=sources,
   310→            confidence=confidence,
   311→            topic=best_topic,
   312→            agent_hint=agent_hint if isinstance(agent_hint, str) else "",
   313→            summary=summary,
   314→            reference_file=ref_file,
   315→        )
   316→
   317→    def _match_reference_sections(
   318→        self, query_lower: str, query_words: set
   319→    ) -> Optional[KnowledgeLookupResult]:
   320→        """Search reference files by section headers using pre-built index."""
   321→        if not self._section_index:
   322→            return None
   323→
   324→        # Gather candidate headers from index (only headers with overlapping words)
   325→        candidates: Dict[tuple, int] = {}  # (file_stem, line_idx) -> overlap count
   326→        candidate_lines: Dict[tuple, list] = {}  # (file_stem, line_idx) -> lines ref
   327→
   328→        for word in query_words:
   329→            for file_stem, line_idx, lines in self._section_index.get(word, []):
   330→                key = (file_stem, line_idx)
   331→                candidates[key] = candidates.get(key, 0) + 1
   332→                if key not in candidate_lines:
   333→                    candidate_lines[key] = lines
   334→
   335→        if not candidates:
   336→            return None
   337→
   338→        # Find best match
   339→        best_key = max(candidates, key=lambda k: candidates[k])
   340→        best_score = candidates[best_key]
   341→
   342→        if best_score < 1:
   343→            return None
   344→
   345→        file_stem, line_idx = best_key
   346→        lines = candidate_lines[best_key]
   347→
   348→        # Extract section content (up to next header or 500 chars)
   349→        section_lines = [lines[line_idx]]
   350→        char_count = len(lines[line_idx])
   351→        for j in range(line_idx + 1, len(lines)):
   352→            if lines[j].startswith("#"):
   353→                break
   354→            section_lines.append(lines[j])
   355→            char_count += len(lines[j])
   356→            if char_count > 500:
   357→                break
   358→
   359→        confidence = min(0.7, 0.3 + 0.15 * best_score)
   360→        return KnowledgeLookupResult(
   361→            found=True,
   362→            answer="\n".join(section_lines),
   363→            sources=[f"reference:{file_stem}"],
   364→            confidence=confidence,
   365→            topic=file_stem,
   366→            reference_file=file_stem,
   367→        )
   368→
   369→    def _match_vex_symptoms(self, query: str) -> Optional[KnowledgeLookupResult]:
   370→        """Match natural-language VEX problem descriptions.
   371→
   372→        Uses symptom patterns from vex_diagnostics to catch artist
   373→        descriptions like 'my points aren't moving' or 'colors look wrong'.
   374→        """
   375→        # Quick gate: only try if the query mentions VEX-related concepts
   376→        _VEX_SIGNALS = {
   377→            "vex", "wrangle", "point", "points", "attrib", "attribute",
   378→            "color", "cd", "orient", "pscale", "scale", "noise",
   379→            "pcfind", "solver", "exploding", "slow", "moving",
   380→        }
   381→        query_words = set(query.lower().split())
   382→        if not query_words & _VEX_SIGNALS:
   383→            return None
   384→
   385→        try:
   386→            from synapse.routing.vex_diagnostics import (
   387→                diagnose_vex_symptom,
   388→                format_diagnosis,
   389→            )
   390→        except ImportError:
   391→            return None
   392→
   393→        diagnoses = diagnose_vex_symptom(query)
   394→        if not diagnoses:
   395→            return None
   396→
   397→        formatted = format_diagnosis(diagnoses)
   398→        best = diagnoses[0]
   399→        return KnowledgeLookupResult(
   400→            found=True,
   401→            answer=formatted,
   402→            sources=[f"vex_diagnostics:{best.reference_topic}"],
   403→            confidence=best.confidence,
   404→            topic=best.reference_topic,
   405→            agent_hint=f"VEX symptom match ({best.category})",
   406→        )
   407→
   408→    def _match_memory(self, query: str) -> Optional[KnowledgeLookupResult]:
   409→        """Search memory as final fallback."""
   410→        if not self._memory:
   411→            return None
   412→
   413→        try:
   414→            results = self._memory.search(text=query, limit=3)
   415→        except Exception:
   416→            return None
   417→
   418→        if not results:
   419→            return None
   420→
   421→        # Use best result if above threshold
   422→        best = results[0]
   423→        if best.score < 0.4:
   424→            return None
   425→
   426→        answer_parts = [best.memory.content]
   427→        if best.memory.summary:
   428→            answer_parts.insert(0, best.memory.summary)
   429→
   430→        sources = [f"memory:{best.memory.id}"]
   431→        for r in results[1:]:
   432→            if r.score >= 0.4:
   433→                sources.append(f"memory:{r.memory.id}")
   434→
   435→        return KnowledgeLookupResult(
   436→            found=True,
   437→            answer="\n".join(answer_parts),
   438→            sources=sources,
   439→            confidence=min(0.8, best.score),
   440→            topic="memory",
   441→            agent_hint="From project memory",
   442→        )
   443→
   444→    @property
   445→    def topic_count(self) -> int:
   446→        """Number of indexed topics."""
   447→        return len(self._semantic_index)
   448→
   449→    @property
   450→    def reference_count(self) -> int:
   451→        """Number of loaded reference files."""
   452→        return len(self._reference_files)
   453→
   454→    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   455→        """Return index statistics."""
   456→        return {
   457→            "topics": self.topic_count,
   458→            "keywords": len(self._keyword_to_topics),
   459→            "references": self.reference_count,
   460→            "has_memory": self._memory is not None,
   461→            "has_rag": self._rag_root is not None,
   462→        }
   463→

1→"""
     2→Synapse Recipe Registry
     3→
     4→Pre-built, pre-approved multi-step operation templates.
     5→Recipes execute at Tier 0 speed by expanding triggers into
     6→sequences of SynapseCommands without any LLM involvement.
     7→
     8→Artists can register custom recipes via registry.register().
     9→"""
    10→
    11→import json
    12→import re
    13→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    14→from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Any
    15→
    16→from ..core.protocol import SynapseCommand
    17→from ..core.gates import GateLevel
    18→from ..core.determinism import deterministic_uuid
    19→
    20→
    21→@dataclass
    22→class RecipeStep:
    23→    """A single step in a recipe template."""
    24→    action: str                        # CommandType value
    25→    payload_template: Dict[str, Any]   # Values may contain {placeholders}
    26→    gate_level: GateLevel = GateLevel.REVIEW
    27→    output_var: str = ""               # If set, response data stored as ${var}.{field}
    28→
    29→    def instantiate(self, params: Dict[str, str]) -> SynapseCommand:
    30→        """Fill placeholders and return a SynapseCommand."""
    31→        payload = {}
    32→        for key, value in sorted(self.payload_template.items()):
    33→            if isinstance(value, str) and "{" in value:
    34→                payload[key] = value.format(**params)
    35→            else:
    36→                payload[key] = value
    37→
    38→        return SynapseCommand(
    39→            type=self.action,
    40→            id=deterministic_uuid(
    41→                f"recipe:{self.action}:{json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str)}", "cmd"
    42→            ),
    43→            payload=payload,
    44→        )
    45→
    46→    def instantiate_with_vars(self, variables: Dict[str, str]) -> SynapseCommand:
    47→        """Fill placeholders using accumulated variables (supports $var.field syntax)."""
    48→        payload = {}
    49→        for key, value in sorted(self.payload_template.items()):
    50→            if isinstance(value, str):
    51→                # Replace $var.field references first
    52→                resolved = value
    53→                for var_key in sorted(variables.keys(), key=len, reverse=True):
    54→                    resolved = resolved.replace(var_key, str(variables[var_key]))
    55→                # Then standard {param} placeholders
    56→                if "{" in resolved:
    57→                    resolved = resolved.format(**{
    58→                        k: v for k, v in sorted(variables.items())
    59→                        if not k.startswith("$")
    60→                    })
    61→                payload[key] = resolved
    62→            else:
    63→                payload[key] = value
    64→
    65→        return SynapseCommand(
    66→            type=self.action,
    67→            id=deterministic_uuid(
    68→                f"recipe:{self.action}:{json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str)}", "cmd"
    69→            ),
    70→            payload=payload,
    71→        )
    72→
    73→
    74→@dataclass
    75→class Recipe:
    76→    """A pre-built multi-step operation template."""
    77→    name: str
    78→    description: str
    79→    triggers: List[str]                # Regex patterns (case-insensitive)
    80→    parameters: List[str]              # Named capture groups expected
    81→    steps: List[RecipeStep]
    82→    gate_level: GateLevel = GateLevel.REVIEW
    83→    category: str = "general"
    84→
    85→    _compiled: List["re.Pattern[str]"] = field(default_factory=list, repr=False)
    86→
    87→    def __post_init__(self):
    88→        self._compiled = [
    89→            re.compile(t, re.IGNORECASE) for t in self.triggers
    90→        ]
    91→
    92→    def match(self, text: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
    93→        """
    94→        Try to match text against trigger patterns.
    95→
    96→        Returns extracted parameters on match, None otherwise.
    97→        """
    98→        text = text.strip()
    99→        for pattern in self._compiled:
   100→            m = pattern.match(text)
   101→            if m:
   102→                params = m.groupdict()
   103→                # Fill defaults for missing optional params
   104→                for p in self.parameters:
   105→                    if p not in params or params[p] is None:
   106→                        params[p] = ""
   107→                return params
   108→        return None
   109→
   110→    def instantiate(self, params: Dict[str, str]) -> List[SynapseCommand]:
   111→        """Fill templates with extracted params, return command list."""
   112→        return [step.instantiate(params) for step in self.steps]
   113→
   114→    def execute(
   115→        self,
   116→        params: Dict[str, str],
   117→        command_fn,
   118→    ) -> List[Tuple[SynapseCommand, Any]]:
   119→        """Execute recipe with data flow between steps.
   120→
   121→        Each step can declare output_var. After execution, response data
   122→        fields become ${var}.{field} variables available to later steps.
   123→
   124→        Args:
   125→            params: Initial parameters from trigger match.
   126→            command_fn: Callable(SynapseCommand) -> SynapseResponse.
   127→
   128→        Returns:
   129→            List of (command, response) tuples.
   130→        """

   132→        results: List[Tuple[SynapseCommand, Any]] = []

   134→            cmd = step.instantiate_with_vars(variables)
   135→            resp = command_fn(cmd)

   139→                    variables[f"${step.output_var}.{k}"] = str(v)
   140→        return results
   141→

   145→    Registry of pre-built recipes.
   146→
   147→    Matches input text against all registered recipes.
   148→    Built-in recipes are registered on construction.

1→"""
     2→Synapse Epoch-Based Tier Adaptation
     3→
     4→Records tier outcomes during each epoch, aggregates success rates at
     5→epoch boundaries, and adjusts confidence thresholds for new (unpinned)
     6→inputs.
     7→
     8→He2025 compliance:
     9→- Fixed epoch SIZE (not time-based) — same as paper's fixed split-size
    10→- sorted() before aggregation — order-independent
    11→- kahan_sum() for float aggregation — stable across batch sizes
    12→- round_float() on output — deterministic precision
    13→- Pin staleness uses epoch ID (monotonic int), not wall-clock time
    14→- No timestamps in any deterministic path
    15→"""
    16→
    17→import logging
    18→import threading
    19→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    20→from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
    21→
    22→from ..core.determinism import kahan_sum, round_float
    23→
    24→logger = logging.getLogger("synapse.routing")
    25→
    26→# Default epoch size — fixed window (not time-based) for stable tier adaptation
    27→DEFAULT_EPOCH_SIZE = 100
    28→
    29→# Thresholds for tier preference adjustment
    30→LOW_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD = 0.5   # Below this, prefer next tier for new queries
    31→HIGH_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD = 0.9  # Above this, prefer this tier more aggressively
    32→
    33→# Number of epochs before a pin is considered stale
    34→PIN_STALE_EPOCHS = 2
    35→
    36→
    37→@dataclass
    38→class TierEpoch:
    39→    """A single epoch of tier outcome observations.
    40→
    41→    Outcomes are collected during the epoch. At the epoch boundary
    42→    (when is_complete is True), aggregate() returns Kahan-summed
    43→    success rates per tier for threshold adjustment.
    44→    """
    45→    epoch_id: int
    46→    epoch_size: int = DEFAULT_EPOCH_SIZE
    47→    outcomes: List[Tuple[str, bool, float]] = field(default_factory=list)
    48→
    49→    def record(self, tier: str, success: bool, latency_ms: float):
    50→        """Record a single tier outcome."""
    51→        self.outcomes.append((tier, success, latency_ms))
    52→
    53→    @property
    54→    def is_complete(self) -> bool:
    55→        """Check if epoch has reached its fixed size."""
    56→        return len(self.outcomes) >= self.epoch_size
    57→
    58→    def aggregate(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
    59→        """Kahan-summed success rates per tier. He2025 compliant.
    60→
    61→        Returns dict mapping tier name to success rate [0.0, 1.0].
    62→        """
    63→        tier_outcomes: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
    64→        for tier, success, _ in sorted(self.outcomes):  # sorted for determinism
    65→            tier_outcomes.setdefault(tier, []).append(1.0 if success else 0.0)
    66→        return {
    67→            tier: round_float(kahan_sum(vals) / len(vals))
    68→            for tier, vals in sorted(tier_outcomes.items())
    69→        }
    70→
    71→    def aggregate_latency(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
    72→        """Kahan-summed average latency per tier in ms."""
    73→        tier_latencies: Dict[str, List[float]] = {}
    74→        for tier, _, latency in sorted(self.outcomes):
    75→            tier_latencies.setdefault(tier, []).append(latency)
    76→        return {
    77→            tier: round_float(kahan_sum(vals) / len(vals))
    78→            for tier, vals in sorted(tier_latencies.items())
    79→        }
    80→
    81→
    82→@dataclass
    83→class TierThresholds:
    84→    """Adjusted confidence thresholds per tier.
    85→
    86→    Higher threshold = tier needs more confidence to be selected
    87→    for new (unpinned) inputs. Range [0.0, 1.0].
    88→    """
    89→    thresholds: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    90→
    91→    def get(self, tier: str, default: float = 0.5) -> float:
    92→        return self.thresholds.get(tier, default)
    93→
    94→    def adjust(self, success_rates: Dict[str, float]):
    95→        """Adjust thresholds based on epoch success rates.
    96→
    97→        Low success -> raise threshold (harder to select).
    98→        High success -> lower threshold (easier to select).
    99→        """
   100→        for tier, rate in sorted(success_rates.items()):
   101→            current = self.thresholds.get(tier, 0.5)
   102→            if rate < LOW_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD:
   103→                # Poor performance — raise threshold (prefer other tiers)
   104→                self.thresholds[tier] = round_float(min(1.0, current + 0.1))
   105→            elif rate > HIGH_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD:
   106→                # Great performance — lower threshold (prefer this tier)
   107→                self.thresholds[tier] = round_float(max(0.1, current - 0.05))
   108→            # Moderate performance — no change
   109→
   110→
   111→class EpochAdapter:
   112→    """Manages epoch lifecycle and threshold adjustment.
   113→
   114→    Thread-safe. One instance per TieredRouter.
   115→    """
   116→
   117→    def __init__(self, epoch_size: int = DEFAULT_EPOCH_SIZE):
   118→        self._epoch_size = epoch_size
   119→        self._current_epoch = TierEpoch(epoch_id=0, epoch_size=epoch_size)
   120→        self._thresholds = TierThresholds()
   121→        self._epoch_history: List[Dict[str, float]] = []  # past epoch aggregates
   122→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
   123→
   124→    @property
   125→    def epoch_id(self) -> int:
   126→        with self._lock:
   127→            return self._current_epoch.epoch_id
   128→
   129→    @property
   130→    def thresholds(self) -> TierThresholds:
   131→        with self._lock:
   132→            return self._thresholds
   133→
   134→    def record(self, tier: str, success: bool, latency_ms: float):
   135→        """Record a tier outcome. If epoch is complete, rotate."""
   136→        with self._lock:
   137→            self._current_epoch.record(tier, success, latency_ms)
   138→            if self._current_epoch.is_complete:
   139→                self._rotate_epoch()
   140→
   141→    def _rotate_epoch(self):
   142→        """Complete current epoch and start a new one.
   143→
   144→        Aggregates success rates, adjusts thresholds, archives.
   145→        Must be called under lock.
   146→        """
   147→        rates = self._current_epoch.aggregate()
   148→        self._epoch_history.append(rates)
   149→        self._thresholds.adjust(rates)
   150→
   151→        logger.info(
   152→            "Epoch %d complete (%d outcomes). Success rates: %s",
   153→            self._current_epoch.epoch_id,
   154→            len(self._current_epoch.outcomes),
   155→            rates,
   156→        )
   157→
   158→        # Start new epoch
   159→        self._current_epoch = TierEpoch(
   160→            epoch_id=self._current_epoch.epoch_id + 1,
   161→            epoch_size=self._epoch_size,
   162→        )
   163→
   164→    def get_stale_pin_epoch(self) -> int:
   165→        """Get the epoch ID below which pins are stale.
   166→
   167→        Pins from epochs older than (current - PIN_STALE_EPOCHS)
   168→        should be evicted.
   169→        """
   170→        with self._lock:
   171→            return max(0, self._current_epoch.epoch_id - PIN_STALE_EPOCHS)
   172→
   173→    def stats(self) -> Dict:
   174→        """Return adaptation statistics."""
   175→        with self._lock:
   176→            return {
   177→                "epoch_id": self._current_epoch.epoch_id,
   178→                "epoch_progress": len(self._current_epoch.outcomes),
   179→                "epoch_size": self._epoch_size,
   180→                "thresholds": dict(sorted(self._thresholds.thresholds.items())),
   181→                "history_epochs": len(self._epoch_history),
   182→                "latest_rates": self._epoch_history[-1] if self._epoch_history else {},
   183→            }
   184→

   507→
   508→                # Keyword scoring

   511→                    if matching_keywords:
   512→                        score += len(matching_keywords) * 0.2
   513→                        match_reasons.append(f"keywords: {', '.join(matching_keywords)}")

   515→                # Text search (still linear over candidates, but candidate set is smaller)

   114→class SQLiteMemoryStore:

     3→
     4→Detects when markdown memory should evolve to USD. Handles the
     5→conversion process and maintains companion markdown.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→import logging
     9→import os
    10→import re
    11→from typing import Dict, List, Any, Optional
    12→
    13→logger = logging.getLogger("synapse.evolution")
    14→
    15→EVOLUTION_TRIGGERS = {
    16→    "charmeleon": {
    17→        "structured_data_count": 5,
    18→        "asset_references": 3,
    19→        "parameter_records": 5,
    20→        "wedge_results": 1,
    21→        "session_count": 10,
    22→        "file_size_kb": 100,
    23→        "node_path_references": 10,
    24→    },
    25→}
    26→
    27→
    28→def count_structured_data(md_path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    29→    """Count structured elements in a markdown memory file."""
    30→    if not os.path.exists(md_path):
    31→        return {k: 0 for k in EVOLUTION_TRIGGERS["charmeleon"]}
    32→
    33→    with open(md_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    34→        content = f.read()
    35→
    36→    lines = content.split("\n")
    37→    counts = {
    38→        "structured_data_count": 0,
    39→        "asset_references": 0,
    40→        "parameter_records": 0,
    41→        "wedge_results": 0,
    42→        "session_count": 0,
    43→        "file_size_kb": round(os.path.getsize(md_path) / 1024, 2),
    44→        "node_path_references": 0,
    45→    }
    46→
    47→    for line in lines:
    48→        # Node paths: /obj/, /stage/, /out/, /shop/
    49→        if re.search(r'/(?:obj|stage|out|shop|ch|mat)/', line):
    50→            counts["node_path_references"] += 1
    51→        # Asset paths: @...@
    52→        if re.search(r'@[^@]+@', line):
    53→            counts["asset_references"] += 1
    54→        # Parameter records: "parm: value" or "Before/After" patterns
    55→        if re.search(r'\*\*(?:Before|After|Value):\*\*', line):
    56→            counts["parameter_records"] += 1
    57→        # Session headers
    58→        if line.startswith("## Session"):
    59→            counts["session_count"] += 1
    60→        # Decision blocks
    61→        if "### Decision:" in line or "**Decision:**" in line:
    62→            counts["structured_data_count"] += 1
    63→        # Wedge results
    64→        if "### Wedge" in line or ("wedge" in line.lower() and "result" in line.lower()):
    65→            counts["wedge_results"] += 1
    66→        # General structured data (node paths, params count as structured)
    67→        if re.search(r'### (?:Parameter|Asset|Blocker)', line):
    68→            counts["structured_data_count"] += 1
    69→
    70→    return counts
    71→
    72→
    73→def check_evolution(claude_dir: str, latest_entry: Dict = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    74→    """
    75→    Evaluate triggers. Return {should_evolve, triggers_met, target}.
    76→    Called after every memory write.
    77→    """
    78→    from .scene_memory import get_evolution_stage
    79→
    80→    stage = get_evolution_stage(claude_dir)
    81→
    82→    if stage != "charmander":
    83→        return {"should_evolve": False, "triggers_met": [], "target": None, "current": stage}
    84→
    85→    md_path = os.path.join(claude_dir, "memory.md")
    86→    counts = count_structured_data(md_path)
    87→    triggers = EVOLUTION_TRIGGERS["charmeleon"]
    88→
    89→    triggers_met = []
    90→    for key, threshold in sorted(triggers.items()):
    91→        if counts.get(key, 0) >= threshold:
    92→            triggers_met.append(key)
    93→
    94→    return {
    95→        "should_evolve": len(triggers_met) > 0,
    96→        "triggers_met": triggers_met,
    97→        "target": "charmeleon" if triggers_met else None,
    98→        "current": stage,
    99→        "counts": counts,
   100→    }
   101→
   102→
   103→def parse_markdown_memory(md_path: str) -> Dict[str, List]:
   104→    """
   105→    Parse memory.md into structured sections.
   106→
   107→    Returns: {sessions, decisions, assets, parameters}
   108→    """
   109→    if not os.path.exists(md_path):
   110→        return {"sessions": [], "decisions": [], "assets": [], "parameters": []}
   111→
   112→    with open(md_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   113→        content = f.read()
   114→
   115→    sessions: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   116→    decisions: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   117→    assets: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   118→    parameters: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   119→
   120→    # Split by ## Session headers
   121→    session_blocks = re.split(r'^## Session ', content, flags=re.MULTILINE)
   122→
   123→    for i, block in enumerate(session_blocks[1:], 1):
   124→        lines = block.strip().split("\n")
   125→        header = lines[0] if lines else ""
   126→        date = header.split()[0] if header else f"session_{i}"
   127→        text = "\n".join(lines)
   128→
   129→        session: Dict[str, Any] = {
   130→            "id": f"session_{date.replace('-', '_')}",
   131→            "date": date,
   132→            "text": text,
   133→            "decisions": [],
   134→            "blockers": [],
   135→            "parameters": [],
   136→        }
   137→
   138→        # Extract decisions within this session
   139→        decision_blocks = re.findall(
   140→            r'### Decision:\s*(.+?)(?=\n###|\n## |\Z)',
   141→            text, re.DOTALL
   142→        )
   143→        for db in decision_blocks:
   144→            decision_lines = db.strip().split("\n")
   145→            name = decision_lines[0].strip() if decision_lines else ""
   146→            choice = ""

   148→            for dl in decision_lines:

   151→                elif dl.startswith("**Reasoning:**"):
   152→                    reasoning = dl.replace("**Reasoning:**", "").strip()
   153→            slug = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', name.lower()).strip('_')[:40]
   154→            decisions.append({
   155→                "slug": slug or f"decision_{len(decisions)}",
   156→                "name": name,
   157→                "choice": choice,
   158→                "reasoning": reasoning,
   159→                "date": date,
   160→                "alternatives": [],
   161→            })
   162→            session["decisions"].append(slug)
   163→
   164→        # Extract parameters
   165→        param_blocks = re.findall(
   166→            r'### Parameter:\s*(.+?)(?=\n###|\n## |\Z)',
   167→            text, re.DOTALL
   168→        )
   169→        for pb in param_blocks:
   170→            param_lines = pb.strip().split("\n")
   171→            header_parts = param_lines[0].strip().split("/") if param_lines else []
   172→            before = after = result = ""
   173→            for pl in param_lines:
   174→                if "**Before:**" in pl:
   175→                    before = pl.split("**Before:**")[-1].strip()
   176→                elif "**After:**" in pl:
   177→                    after = pl.split("**After:**")[-1].strip()
   178→                elif "**Result:**" in pl:
   179→                    result = pl.split("**Result:**")[-1].strip()
   180→            slug = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', param_lines[0].strip().lower()).strip('_')[:40]
   181→            parameters.append({
   182→                "slug": slug or f"param_{len(parameters)}",
   183→                "node": "/".join(header_parts[:-1]) if len(header_parts) > 1 else "",
   184→                "parm": header_parts[-1].strip() if header_parts else "",
   185→                "before": before,
   186→                "after": after,
   187→                "result": result,
   188→                "date": date,
   189→            })
   190→            session["parameters"].append(slug)
   191→
   192→        sessions.append(session)
   193→
   194→    return {
   195→        "sessions": sessions,
   196→        "decisions": decisions,
   197→        "assets": assets,
   198→        "parameters": parameters,
   199→    }
   200→
   201→
   202→def evolve_to_charmeleon(md_path: str, usd_path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   203→    """

    56→    Returns:

    71→    t0 = time.monotonic()
