   445→    def search(self, query: MemoryQuery) -> List[MemorySearchResult]:
   446→        """Search memories based on query parameters.
   447→
   448→        Uses the in-memory index to narrow candidates before scoring,
   449→        avoiding a full scan when type/tag/keyword filters are provided.
   450→        Falls back to full scan only for pure text queries.
   451→        """
   452→        self._wait_loaded()
   453→        with self._lock.read_lock():
   454→            # --- Candidate narrowing via index ---
   455→            candidates = None  # None = "all", set() = "none matched yet"
   456→
   457→            if query.memory_types:
   458→                type_ids: set = set()
   459→                for mt in query.memory_types:
   460→                    type_ids.update(self._index["by_type"].get(mt.value, []))
   461→                candidates = type_ids
   462→
   463→            if query.tags:
   464→                tag_ids: set = set()
   465→                for tag in query.tags:
   466→                    tag_ids.update(self._index["by_tag"].get(tag, []))
   467→                candidates = tag_ids if candidates is None else candidates & tag_ids
   468→
   469→            if query.keywords:
   470→                kw_ids: set = set()
   471→                for kw in query.keywords:
   472→                    kw_ids.update(self._index["by_keyword"].get(kw, []))
   473→                candidates = kw_ids if candidates is None else candidates & kw_ids
   474→
   475→            # Resolve candidate IDs to Memory objects
   476→            if candidates is not None:
   477→                pool = [self._memories[mid] for mid in candidates if mid in self._memories]
   478→            else:
   479→                pool = list(self._memories.values())
   480→
   481→            # --- Score candidates ---
   482→            results = []
   483→
   484→            for memory in pool:
   485→                if memory.is_consolidated and not query.include_consolidated:
   486→                    continue
   487→
   488→                # Post-filter: tier, source, time range
   489→                if query.tier and memory.tier != query.tier:
   490→                    continue
   491→                if query.source and memory.source != query.source:
   492→                    continue
   493→                if query.since and memory.created_at < query.since:
   494→                    continue
   495→                if query.until and memory.created_at > query.until:
   496→                    continue
   497→
   498→                score = 0.0
   499→                match_reasons = []
   500→
   501→                # Tag scoring (index already filtered, but score the overlap)
   502→                if query.tags:
   503→                    matching_tags = set(query.tags) & set(memory.tags)
   504→                    if matching_tags:
   505→                        score += len(matching_tags) * 0.2
   506→                        match_reasons.append(f"tags: {', '.join(matching_tags)}")
   507→
   508→                # Keyword scoring
   509→                if query.keywords:
   510→                    matching_keywords = set(query.keywords) & set(memory.keywords)
   511→                    if matching_keywords:
   512→                        score += len(matching_keywords) * 0.2
   513→                        match_reasons.append(f"keywords: {', '.join(matching_keywords)}")
   514→
   515→                # Text search (still linear over candidates, but candidate set is smaller)
   516→                if query.text:
   517→                    text_lower = query.text.lower()
   518→                    content_lower = memory.content.lower()
   519→                    summary_lower = memory.summary.lower()
   520→
   521→                    if text_lower in content_lower:
   522→                        score += 0.5
   523→                        match_reasons.append("content match")
   524→                    if text_lower in summary_lower:
   525→                        score += 0.3
   526→                        match_reasons.append("summary match")
   527→
   528→                    words = text_lower.split()
   529→                    word_matches = sum(1 for w in words if w in content_lower or w in summary_lower)
   530→                    if word_matches > 0:
   531→                        score += word_matches * 0.1
   532→                        match_reasons.append(f"{word_matches} word matches")
   533→
   534→                # No criteria = return all with base score
   535→                if not query.text and not query.tags and not query.keywords:
   536→                    score = 0.5
   537→
   538→                if score > 0:
   539→                    results.append(MemorySearchResult(
   540→                        memory=memory,
   541→                        score=min(1.0, score),
   542→                        match_reasons=match_reasons
   543→                    ))
   544→
   545→            # He2025: stable sort with ID tiebreaker for deterministic ordering
   546→            results.sort(key=lambda r: (-r.score, r.memory.id))
   547→
   548→            if query.limit > 0:
   549→                results = results[:query.limit]
   550→
   551→            return results
   552→
   553→    def get_by_type(self, memory_type: MemoryType) -> List[Memory]:
   554→        """Get all memories of a specific type."""
   555→        self._wait_loaded()
   556→        with self._lock.read_lock():
   557→            ids = self._index["by_type"].get(memory_type.value, [])
   558→            return [self._memories[id] for id in ids if id in self._memories]
   559→
   560→    def get_by_tag(self, tag: str) -> List[Memory]:
   561→        """Get all memories with a specific tag."""
   562→        self._wait_loaded()
   563→        with self._lock.read_lock():
   564→            ids = self._index["by_tag"].get(tag.lower(), [])
   565→            return [self._memories[id] for id in ids if id in self._memories]
   566→
   567→    def get_linked(self, memory_id: str) -> List[Memory]:
   568→        """Get all memories linked to a specific memory."""
   569→        self._wait_loaded()
   570→        with self._lock.read_lock():
   571→            links = self._index["links"].get(memory_id, [])
   572→            return [
   573→                self._memories[link["target"]]
   574→                for link in links
   575→                if link["target"] in self._memories
   576→            ]
   577→
   578→    def get_recent(self, limit: int = 10) -> List[Memory]:
   579→        """Get most recent memories."""
   580→        self._wait_loaded()
   581→        with self._lock.read_lock():
   582→            sorted_memories = sorted(
   583→                self._memories.values(),
   584→                key=lambda m: m.created_at,
   585→                reverse=True
   586→            )
   587→            return sorted_memories[:limit]

   593→
   594→class SynapseMemory:
   595→    """
   596→    High-level API for Synapse memory system.
   597→
   598→    Automatically detects current Houdini project and manages memory storage.
   599→    Provides convenient methods for common operations.
   600→
   601→    Migration: Automatically migrates .nexus/ or .engram/ to .synapse/ if needed.
   602→    """
   603→
   604→    def __init__(self, project_path: Optional[str] = None):
   605→        """
   606→        Initialize Synapse for a project.
   607→
   608→        Args:
   609→            project_path: Optional path to .hip file or project directory.
   610→                         If None, uses current Houdini project.
   611→        """
   612→        self.project_path = self._resolve_project_path(project_path)
   613→        self.storage_dir = self._get_storage_dir()
   614→        self.store = MemoryStore(self.storage_dir)
   615→
   616→        # Callbacks
   617→        self._on_memory_added: List[Callable[[Memory], None]] = []
   618→        self._on_memory_updated: List[Callable[[Memory], None]] = []
   619→
   620→        logger.info("Initialized for project: %s", self.project_path)
   621→        logger.info("Storage: %s", self.storage_dir)
   622→
   623→    def _resolve_project_path(self, path: Optional[str]) -> Path:
   624→        """Resolve the project path."""
   625→        if path:
   626→            return Path(path)
   627→
   628→        if HOU_AVAILABLE:
   629→            hip_path = hou.hipFile.path()
   630→            if hip_path and hip_path != "untitled.hip":
   631→                return Path(hip_path)
   632→            else:
   633→                # Use temp directory for unsaved projects
   634→                return Path(hou.text.expandString("$HOUDINI_TEMP_DIR")) / "untitled"
   635→
   636→        # Fallback
   637→        return Path.cwd() / "untitled.hip"
   638→
   639→    def _get_storage_dir(self) -> Path:
   640→        """
   641→        Get the storage directory for this project.
   642→
   643→        3-tier migration logic:
   644→        1. If .synapse/ exists -> use it
   645→        2. If .nexus/ exists -> copy to .synapse/, leave marker
   646→        3. If .engram/ exists -> copy to .synapse/, leave marker
   647→        4. Otherwise -> create .synapse/
   648→        """
   649→        if self.project_path.is_file():
   650→            base_dir = self.project_path.parent
   651→        else:
   652→            base_dir = self.project_path
   653→
   654→        synapse_dir = base_dir / ".synapse"
   655→        nexus_dir = base_dir / ".nexus"
   656→        engram_dir = base_dir / ".engram"
   657→
   658→        # Priority 1: Use existing .synapse/
   659→        if synapse_dir.exists():
   660→            return synapse_dir
   661→
   662→        # Priority 2: Migrate from .nexus/
   663→        if nexus_dir.exists():
   664→            try:
   665→                logger.info("Migrating from .nexus/ to .synapse/")
   666→                shutil.copytree(nexus_dir, synapse_dir)
   667→                migration_marker = nexus_dir / ".migrated_to_synapse"
   668→                migration_marker.write_text(
   669→                    f"Migrated to .synapse/ on {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n"
   670→                    f"This directory is kept for backwards compatibility.\n"
   671→                    f"You can safely delete it."
   672→                )
   673→                logger.info("Migration complete: %s -> %s", nexus_dir, synapse_dir)
   674→                return synapse_dir
   675→            except Exception as e:
   676→                logger.warning("Migration failed: %s. Using .nexus/ directly.", e)
   677→                return nexus_dir
   678→
   679→        # Priority 3: Migrate from .engram/
   680→        if engram_dir.exists():
   681→            try:
   682→                logger.info("Migrating from .engram/ to .synapse/")
   683→                shutil.copytree(engram_dir, synapse_dir)
   684→                migration_marker = engram_dir / ".migrated_to_synapse"
   685→                migration_marker.write_text(
   686→                    f"Migrated to .synapse/ on {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n"
   687→                    f"This directory is kept for backwards compatibility.\n"
   688→                    f"You can safely delete it."
   689→                )
   690→                logger.info("Migration complete: %s -> %s", engram_dir, synapse_dir)
   691→                return synapse_dir
   692→            except Exception as e:
   693→                logger.warning("Migration failed: %s. Using .engram/ directly.", e)
   694→                return engram_dir
   695→
   696→        # Priority 4: Create new .synapse/
   697→        return synapse_dir

   699→    def add(
   700→        self,
   701→        content: str,
   702→        memory_type: MemoryType = MemoryType.NOTE,
   703→        tags: List[str] = None,
   704→        keywords: List[str] = None,
   705→        source: str = "user",
   706→        node_paths: List[str] = None,
   707→        links: List[Dict] = None
   708→    ) -> Memory:
   709→        """
   710→        Add a new memory.
   711→
   712→        Args:
   713→            content: The memory content
   714→            memory_type: Type of memory
   715→            tags: Categorical tags
   716→            keywords: Key concepts
   717→            source: Who created this ("user", "ai", "auto")
   718→            node_paths: Related Houdini node paths
   719→            links: Links to other memories [{"target_id": "...", "type": "...", "reason": "..."}]
   720→
   721→        Returns:
   722→            The created Memory object
   723→        """
   724→        # Get Houdini context if available
   725→        hip_file = ""
   726→        hip_version = 0
   727→        frame = None
   728→
   729→        if HOU_AVAILABLE:
   730→            hip_file = hou.hipFile.name()
   731→            # Try to extract version from filename
   732→            try:
   733→                import re
   734→                version_match = re.search(r'_v(\d+)', hip_file)
   735→                if version_match:
   736→                    hip_version = int(version_match.group(1))
   737→            except:
   738→                pass
   739→            frame = int(hou.frame())
   740→
   741→        # Create memory
   742→        memory = Memory(
   743→            content=content,
   744→            memory_type=memory_type,
   745→            tier=MemoryTier.SHOT,
   746→            tags=tags or [],
   747→            keywords=keywords or [],
   748→            source=source,
   749→            hip_file=hip_file,
   750→            hip_version=hip_version,
   751→            frame=frame,
   752→            node_paths=node_paths or []
   753→        )
   754→
   755→        # Add links
   756→        if links:
   757→            for link_data in links:
   758→                memory.add_link(
   759→                    target_id=link_data["target_id"],
   760→                    link_type=LinkType(link_data.get("type", "related")),
   761→                    reason=link_data.get("reason", "")
   762→                )
   763→
   764→        # Store
   765→        self.store.add(memory)
   766→
   767→        # Notify callbacks
   768→        for callback in self._on_memory_added:
   769→            try:
   770→                callback(memory)
   771→            except Exception as e:
   772→                logger.error("Callback error: %s", e)
   773→
   774→        return memory

   890→    def _extract_keywords(self, text: str, max_keywords: int = 5) -> List[str]:
   891→        """Simple keyword extraction from text."""
   892→        # Remove common words
   893→        stop_words = {
   894→            'the', 'a', 'an', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'be', 'been',
   895→            'being', 'have', 'has', 'had', 'do', 'does', 'did', 'will',
   896→            'would', 'could', 'should', 'may', 'might', 'must', 'shall',
   897→            'can', 'need', 'dare', 'ought', 'used', 'to', 'of', 'in',
   898→            'for', 'on', 'with', 'at', 'by', 'from', 'as', 'into',
   899→            'through', 'during', 'before', 'after', 'above', 'below',
   900→            'between', 'under', 'again', 'further', 'then', 'once',
   901→            'and', 'but', 'or', 'nor', 'so', 'yet', 'both', 'either',
   902→            'neither', 'not', 'only', 'same', 'than', 'too', 'very',
   903→            'just', 'also', 'now', 'here', 'there', 'when', 'where',
   904→            'why', 'how', 'all', 'each', 'every', 'both', 'few', 'more',
   905→            'most', 'other', 'some', 'such', 'no', 'any', 'this', 'that',
   906→            'these', 'those', 'what', 'which', 'who', 'whom', 'whose'
   907→        }
   908→
   909→        # Tokenize and filter
   910→        words = text.lower().split()
   911→        words = [w.strip('.,!?;:()[]{}"\'-') for w in words]
   912→        words = [w for w in words if w and len(w) > 2 and w not in stop_words]
   913→
   914→        # Count frequencies
   915→        freq: Dict[str, int] = {}
   916→        for w in words:
   917→            freq[w] = freq.get(w, 0) + 1
   918→
   919→        # Return top keywords
   920→        sorted_words = sorted(freq.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
   921→        return [w for w, _ in sorted_words[:max_keywords]]

```python
        with self._write_lock:

        try:
```

```python
import sys

from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch, mock_open, MagicMock

_base = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "python" / "synapse"

# Stub hou module
if "hou" not in sys.modules:
    sys.modules["hou"] = types.ModuleType("hou")


class TestFlushResilience:
    """C3: Buffer restored on write failure."""

    def test_buffer_restored_on_write_failure(self, tmp_path):
        """If disk write fails, buffer lines are restored for retry."""
        # Import store module
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
            "synapse.memory.store", _base / "memory" / "store.py"
        )
        store_mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(store_mod)

        original_open = open
        def failing_open(path, mode='r', **kwargs):
            if 'a' in mode:
                raise OSError("Disk full")
            return original_open(path, mode, **kwargs)

        with patch("builtins.open", side_effect=failing_open):
            store._flush_writes()

        # Buffer should be restored
        assert len(store._write_buffer) == 2

        """Normal flush clears the buffer."""

        spec.loader.exec_module(store_mod)

        store = store_mod.MemoryStore(storage_dir=str(tmp_path))
        # Create the memory file first
        (tmp_path / "memory.jsonl").touch()
        store._write_buffer = ['{"id": "1"}\n']
        store._flush_writes()
        assert len(store._write_buffer) == 0

    """C4: Stale index.json doesn't overwrite live index."""

        """After loading JSONL, stale index.json doesn't replace live index."""
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
            "synapse.memory.store", _base / "memory" / "store.py"
        )
        store_mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(store_mod)

        # Write 3 memories to JSONL
        mem_file = tmp_path / "memory.jsonl"
        for i in range(3):
            entry = {
                "id": f"mem-{i}",
                "memory_type": "observation",
                "content": f"test {i}",
                "tags": [f"tag{i}"],
                "timestamp": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
                "metadata": {},

            with open(mem_file, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f:

        )

        wait_pos = source.index("wait(")
        assert clear_pos < wait_pos, "clear() must come before wait() to prevent signal loss"
```

### C3: Fix buffer data loss on flush failure

**File**: `python/synapse/memory/store.py` — find `_flush_writes()` method (around line 224-236)

**Bug**: Buffer is cleared BEFORE the write. If `f.write()` fails (disk full), data is gone forever.

**Fix**: On write failure, restore lines back to buffer:

```python
    def _flush_writes(self):
        """Flush buffered memory lines to disk."""
        with self._write_lock:
            if not self._write_buffer:
                return
            lines = self._write_buffer[:]
            self._write_buffer.clear()

        try:
            with open(self.memory_file, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write("".join(lines))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error("Write flush error, restoring %d lines to buffer: %s", len(lines), e)
            with self._write_lock:
                # Prepend failed lines back (they're older than anything new)
                self._write_buffer[0:0] = lines
```

```python
    def _flush_writes(self):
        """Flush buffered memory lines to disk."""
        with self._write_lock:
            if not self._write_buffer:
                return
            lines = self._write_buffer[:]
            self._write_buffer.clear()

        try:
            with open(self.memory_file, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write("".join(lines))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error("Write flush error, restoring %d lines to buffer: %s", len(lines), e)
            with self._write_lock:

                self._write_buffer[0:0] = lines
```

```python
    def _flush_loop(self):
```

```python
        store = store_mod.MemoryStore(storage_dir=str(tmp_path))
        # Create the memory file first
        (tmp_path / "memory.jsonl").touch()
        store._write_buffer = ['{"id": "1"}\n']
        store._flush_writes()
        assert len(store._write_buffer) == 0

        assert len(obs_set) == 3


class TestFlushEventOrdering:

        assert clear_pos < wait_pos, "clear() must come before wait() to prevent signal loss"
```

**File**: `python/synapse/mcp/session.py`

The `MCPSessionManager` class creates sessions but NEVER cleans them up. No expiry, no max count. This is a resource leak.

Add these constants after the existing module-level constants:

Add a `_sweep_expired()` method to `MCPSessionManager` and call it from `create_session()`:

```python
    def create_session(self, client_info: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
        """Create a new session. Sweeps expired sessions first."""
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

```python
    def _sweep_expired(self):

        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
```

All three fixes are applied and all 204 tests pass (198 existing + 6 new). Here is a summary of what was done:

---

## Changes Applied

### C2: Fix `future.result()` -- add try/except and timeout

**File**: `C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE\python\synapse\routing\router.py` (lines 317-318)

The speculative T0+T1 parallelism section called `t0_future.result()` and `t1_lookup_future.result()` with no exception handling and no timeout. If either future raised (e.g., knowledge index corrupted, regex engine crash), the entire `route()` method would propagate the exception to the caller. Now each `future.result()` is wrapped in `try/except Exception` with a 2-second timeout, logging a warning and setting the result to `None` on failure so the cascade falls through gracefully.

### C6: Fix tier pin TOCTOU -- re-check value before delete

**File**: `C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE\python\synapse\routing\router.py` (lines 262-264)

The stale pin deletion path had a time-of-check-to-time-of-use race: thread A reads `pinned_tier="recipe"`, the pinned tier returns `None` (stale), but between the read and the write-lock acquisition, thread B could update the pin to `"instant"`. The old code unconditionally deleted the pin, destroying thread B's valid update. The fix adds a value guard: `if self._tier_pins.get(pin_key) == pinned_tier` before the `pop()`, so deletion only proceeds if the value is still what thread A originally read.

### C10: Cap `_epoch_history` growth

**File**: `C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE\python\synapse\routing\adaptation.py`

`_epoch_history` was an unbounded `List` that grew by one entry every `epoch_size` outcomes. Over long sessions this could consume unbounded memory. Changed to `collections.deque(maxlen=100)` which automatically evicts the oldest epoch when the cap is reached. Added constant `_MAX_EPOCH_HISTORY = 100`. The existing `.append()` call and `len()` usage work identically with `deque`.

### C2t, C6t, C10t: Tests added to `tests/test_routing.py`

Six new tests across three test classes:

- **`TestSpeculativeParallelismResilience`** (2 tests): Verifies that exceptions in `knowledge.lookup()` and `_try_tier0()` during parallel execution don't crash routing -- the cascade falls through gracefully.
- **`TestTierPinTOCTOU`** (2 tests): Verifies that a stale pin deletion preserves a newer pin value written by another thread, and that deletion proceeds normally when the value is unchanged.
- **`TestEpochHistoryBounded`** (2 tests): Verifies that after 250 epoch rotations the history stays capped at 100 entries, and confirms the backing type is a `deque` with `maxlen=100`.

All three fixes are applied and all 204 tests pass (198 existing + 6 new). Here is a summary of what was done:

---

## Changes Applied

### C2: Fix `future.result()` -- add try/except and timeout

**File**: `C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE\python\synapse\routing\router.py` (lines 317-318)

The speculative T0+T1 parallelism section called `t0_future.result()` and `t1_lookup_future.result()` with no exception handling and no timeout. If either future raised (e.g., knowledge index corrupted, regex engine crash), the entire `route()` method would propagate the exception to the caller. Now each `future.result()` is wrapped in `try/except Exception` with a 2-second timeout, logging a warning and setting the result to `None` on failure so the cascade falls through gracefully.

### C6: Fix tier pin TOCTOU -- re-check value before delete

**File**: `C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE\python\synapse\routing\router.py` (lines 262-264)

The stale pin deletion path had a time-of-check-to-time-of-use race: thread A reads `pinned_tier="recipe"`, the pinned tier returns `None` (stale), but between the read and the write-lock acquisition, thread B could update the pin to `"instant"`. The old code unconditionally deleted the pin, destroying thread B's valid update. The fix adds a value guard: `if self._tier_pins.get(pin_key) == pinned_tier` before the `pop()`, so deletion only proceeds if the value is still what thread A originally read.

### C10: Cap `_epoch_history` growth

**File**: `C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE\python\synapse\routing\adaptation.py`

`_epoch_history` was an unbounded `List` that grew by one entry every `epoch_size` outcomes. Over long sessions this could consume unbounded memory. Changed to `collections.deque(maxlen=100)` which automatically evicts the oldest epoch when the cap is reached. Added constant `_MAX_EPOCH_HISTORY = 100`. The existing `.append()` call and `len()` usage work identically with `deque`.

### C2t, C6t, C10t: Tests added to `tests/test_routing.py`

Six new tests across three test classes:

- **`TestSpeculativeParallelismResilience`** (2 tests): Verifies that exceptions in `knowledge.lookup()` and `_try_tier0()` during parallel execution don't crash routing -- the cascade falls through gracefully.
- **`TestTierPinTOCTOU`** (2 tests): Verifies that a stale pin deletion preserves a newer pin value written by another thread, and that deletion proceeds normally when the value is unchanged.
- **`TestEpochHistoryBounded`** (2 tests): Verifies that after 250 epoch rotations the history stays capped at 100 entries, and confirms the backing type is a `deque` with `maxlen=100`.

```python
import threading

_alias_lock = threading.Lock()

def add_alias(canonical: str, alias: str):
    """Add a new alias for a canonical parameter name. Thread-safe."""
    with _alias_lock:
        if canonical not in PARAM_ALIASES:
            PARAM_ALIASES[canonical] = [canonical]
        if alias not in PARAM_ALIASES[canonical]:
            PARAM_ALIASES[canonical].append(alias)
        # Keep reverse map in sync
```

### C9: Add session expiry to MCPSessionManager

The `MCPSessionManager` class creates sessions but NEVER cleans them up. No expiry, no max count. This is a resource leak.

```python
    def create_session(self, client_info: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
        """Create a new session. Sweeps expired sessions first."""
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

**File**: `python/synapse/memory/store.py` — find `_flush_writes()` method (around line 224-236)

**Bug**: Buffer is cleared BEFORE the write. If `f.write()` fails (disk full), data is gone forever.

**Fix**: On write failure, restore lines back to buffer:

```python
    def _flush_writes(self):
        """Flush buffered memory lines to disk."""
        with self._write_lock:
            if not self._write_buffer:
                return
            lines = self._write_buffer[:]
            self._write_buffer.clear()

        try:
            with open(self.memory_file, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write("".join(lines))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error("Write flush error, restoring %d lines to buffer: %s", len(lines), e)
            with self._write_lock:
                # Prepend failed lines back (they're older than anything new)
                self._write_buffer[0:0] = lines
```

**File**: `python/synapse/memory/store.py` — find the `_load()` method, specifically the block around lines 276-293 where `self._index = loaded` is set.

**Bug**: After loading memories from JSONL and building a fresh in-memory index via `_index_memory()`, the code loads `index.json` and OVERWRITES the fresh index with a potentially stale one.

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:

            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()

            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)

```python
        with self._lock:

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

```python
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
```

```python
        """Create a new session. Sweeps expired sessions first."""
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

```python
    def create_session(self, client_info: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
        """Create a new session. Sweeps expired sessions first."""
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

```python
    def _sweep_expired(self):

        with self._lock:

            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
```

```python
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:

            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
```

### C9: Add session expiry to MCPSessionManager

```python
    def create_session(self, client_info: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
        """Create a new session. Sweeps expired sessions first."""
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

```python
    def create_session(self, client_info: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
        """Create a new session. Sweeps expired sessions first."""
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

```python
    def _sweep_expired(self):

        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:

            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()

            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
```

```python
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

```python
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
```

### C9: Add session expiry to MCPSessionManager

**File**: `python/synapse/mcp/session.py`

The `MCPSessionManager` class creates sessions but NEVER cleans them up. No expiry, no max count. This is a resource leak.

```python
    def create_session(self, client_info: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
        """Create a new session. Sweeps expired sessions first."""
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL
            ]
            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

```python
    def _sweep_expired(self):

        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
```

```python
    def create_session(self, client_info: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
        """Create a new session. Sweeps expired sessions first."""
        self._sweep_expired()
        session_id = _next_session_id()
        session = MCPSession(session_id, client_info or {})
        with self._lock:
            self._sessions[session_id] = session
        return session_id

    def _sweep_expired(self):
        """Remove sessions older than TTL and enforce max count."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            # Remove expired
            expired = [
                sid for sid, s in self._sessions.items()
                if (now - s.created_at) > _SESSION_TTL

            for sid in expired:
                del self._sessions[sid]
            # Enforce max count (remove oldest first)
            if len(self._sessions) > _MAX_SESSIONS:
                by_age = sorted(self._sessions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].created_at)
                excess = len(self._sessions) - _MAX_SESSIONS
                for sid, _ in by_age[:excess]:
                    del self._sessions[sid]
```

   133→## Architecture
   134→
   135→### Data Flow (MCP to Houdini)
   136→
   137→```
   138→ANY MCP Client (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, custom agents)
   139→    |  Streamable HTTP: POST/GET http://localhost:PORT/mcp
   140→    |  JSON-RPC 2.0 + Mcp-Session-Id headers
   141→    |
   142→MCP Protocol Layer  (synapse/mcp/)
   143→    |  Session mgmt, tool/resource/prompt dispatch
   144→    |  Translates JSON-RPC ↔ SYNAPSE commands
   145→    |
   146→    ├─── tools/call ──────┐
   147→    ├─── resources/read ──┤
   148→    └─── prompts/get ─────┤
   149→                          |
   150→Claude Desktop/Code       |  (existing stdio path preserved)
   151→    |  stdio / JSON-RPC   |
   152→mcp_server.py  (107 tools) |
   153→    |                     |
   154→    ├─────────────────────┘
   155→    |  WebSocket: ws://localhost:9999/synapse
   156→SynapseServer  (daemon thread inside Houdini)
   157→    |  CommandHandlerRegistry (handlers.py)
   158→hou.* Python API
   159→    |
   160→Houdini USD Stage / Solaris / Karma
   161→```
   162→
   163→Both MCP Streamable HTTP and the existing WebSocket/stdio paths converge at the same handler layer. The MCP protocol layer adds no new safety logic — it delegates entirely to existing handlers which enforce atomic scripts, idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions.

   180→### Routing Cascade (cheapest-first)
   181→
   182→```
   183→Cache(O(1)) -> Recipe(O(1)) -> Planner(O(1)) -> Tier0/regex(O(n)) -> Tier1/RAG(O(log n)) -> Tier2/Haiku(~5s) -> Tier3/Agent(~15s)
   184→```
   185→
   186→- **Tier pinning** (He2025 consistency): Same input+context maps to same tier on subsequent calls. LRU cache, max 1,000 pins, stale pins fall through.
   187→- **Speculative T0+T1 parallelism**: Module-level `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)` runs Tier 0 regex and Tier 1 knowledge lookup concurrently.
   188→- **Tier 1 result threading**: `route()` runs `knowledge.lookup()` once, threads the result to all higher tiers to avoid redundant lookups.
   189→
   190→### Transport Backends
   191→
   192→| Backend | Module | Transport | Latency | Use Case |
   193→|---------|--------|-----------|---------|----------|
   194→| `websockets` | `server/websocket.py` | WebSocket | ~0.2ms warm ping | Primary — reads, pings, everything |
   195→| `hwebserver` | `server/hwebserver_adapter.py` | HTTP (Houdini native) | ~2s floor (main event loop) | Optional — only for hou.* mutations |
   196→| `mcp` | `mcp/server.py` | Streamable HTTP (MCP) | ~2s (hwebserver) | Universal MCP client access (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, etc.) |
   197→
   198→WebSocket remains the primary internal transport. The MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint is additive — it provides a standardized protocol interface that any MCP-compliant client can use. Both share the same handler layer.
   199→
   200→### Authentication (`server/auth.py`)
   201→
   202→Optional API key authentication for both transports. Key sources (checked in order):
   203→1. `SYNAPSE_API_KEY` environment variable
   204→2. `~/.synapse/auth.key` file (first non-empty, non-comment line)
   205→3. No key configured -> auth disabled (backward compat)
   206→
   207→When enabled, first WebSocket message must be an `authenticate` command with `{"payload": {"key": "..."}}`. Uses `hmac.compare_digest` for constant-time comparison. Auth handshake integrated into both `websocket.py` and `hwebserver_adapter.py`.
   208→
   209→**MCP auth (Phase 3):** Bearer token authentication via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on the `/mcp` endpoint. Opt-in for remote/studio deployments. Not required for localhost connections. Implemented as a `TokenVerifier` that delegates to the existing `auth.py` key validation.
   210→
   211→### MCP Server — stdio Bridge (`mcp_server.py`)
   212→
   213→107 tools (36 houdini_, 34 synapse_, 17 tops_, 20 cops_). Key operational details:
   214→- **Concurrent dispatch**: `_pending` dict + `_recv_loop` coroutine — no blocking lock, true parallel tool calls
   215→- **Timeouts**: Default 10s. Overrides: execute_python/execute_vex/capture_viewport/inspect_* at 30s, render/wedge at 120s, batch at 60s
   216→- **JSON**: Uses `orjson` (fast, sort_keys via `OPT_SORT_KEYS`) when available, falls back to stdlib `json`
   217→- **Warmup**: Pre-connect in `main()` reduces first-call latency
   218→- **Retry**: `MAX_RETRIES=2`, `RETRY_DELAY=0.3`, auto-retry on connection drop
   219→- **Connection**: `open_timeout=3.0`, `ping_interval=None`, `compression=None` (localhost optimization)
   220→
   221→The stdio MCP bridge (`mcp_server.py`) and the Streamable HTTP layer (`synapse/mcp/`) are separate transports sharing the same handler layer.
   222→
   223→### MCP Protocol Layer — Streamable HTTP
   224→
   225→The MCP protocol layer lives in `synapse/mcp/` and provides a JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint at `/mcp` on the hwebserver.
   226→
   227→#### Endpoint Behavior
   228→
   229→```
   230→POST /mcp   →  Client sends JSON-RPC request or notification
   231→               Response: application/json (single result) or text/event-stream (streaming)
   232→GET  /mcp   →  Opens optional SSE stream for server→client messages (Phase 3)
   233→```
   234→
   235→#### Session Lifecycle
   236→
   237→1. Client POSTs `initialize` with `clientInfo` and `protocolVersion`
   238→2. Server responds with capabilities, serverInfo, and `Mcp-Session-Id` header
   239→3. Client sends `notifications/initialized` (server returns 202 Accepted)
   240→4. Session is live — client can call `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/read`, etc.
   241→5. Session ends when client disconnects or sends `notifications/cancelled`
   242→
   243→#### Initialize Response
   244→
   245→```python
   246→{
   247→    "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
   248→    "capabilities": {
   249→        "tools": {"listChanged": True},
   250→        "resources": {"subscribe": False, "listChanged": False},
   251→    },
   252→    "serverInfo": {
   253→        "name": "synapse",
   254→        "version": "5.7.0"
   255→    },
   256→    "instructions": (
   257→        "SYNAPSE is a bridge between AI agents and SideFX Houdini. "
   258→        "All mutations go through safety middleware enforcing atomic scripts, "
   259→        "idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions. "
   260→        "Tools marked destructiveHint=True modify the Houdini scene."
   261→    )
   262→}
   263→```
   264→
   265→#### Tool Registry — Mapping Existing Handlers
   266→
   267→Every existing SYNAPSE command handler maps 1:1 to an MCP tool. The `synapse/mcp/tools.py` module builds `tools/list` output from handler introspection and dispatches `tools/call` to the handler registry.
   268→
   269→Tool definitions include JSON Schema `inputSchema` and MCP `annotations`:
   270→
   271→```python
   272→{
   273→    "name": "execute_vex",
   274→    "description": "Execute VEX code on a wrangle node through SYNAPSE safety middleware.",
   275→    "inputSchema": {
   276→        "type": "object",
   277→        "properties": {
   278→            "code": {"type": "string", "description": "VEX source code"},
   279→            "node_path": {"type": "string", "description": "Full path to wrangle node"},
   280→            "run_over": {
   281→                "type": "string",
   282→                "enum": ["Points", "Vertices", "Primitives", "Detail"],
   283→                "default": "Points"
   284→            }
   285→        },
   286→        "required": ["code", "node_path"]
   287→    },
   288→    "annotations": {
   289→        "title": "Execute VEX Code",
   290→        "readOnlyHint": False,
   291→        "destructiveHint": True,
   292→        "idempotentHint": False,
   293→        "openWorldHint": False
   294→    }
   295→}
   296→```
   297→
   298→**Annotation rules:** Use `readOnlyHint: True` for all read/inspect/get operations. Use `destructiveHint: True` for anything that modifies the scene. Use `idempotentHint: True` for set operations where repeat calls produce the same result. MCP clients use these for UI gating and safety decisions.
   299→
   300→#### Tool Dispatch — Bridge to Handlers
   301→
   302→```python
   303→async def dispatch_tool(tool_name: str, arguments: dict) -> dict:
   304→    """Bridge MCP tools/call to existing SYNAPSE handlers.
   305→    Safety middleware is enforced by the handlers — NOT bypassed."""
   306→    handler = HANDLER_REGISTRY.get(tool_name)
   307→    if not handler:
   308→        raise MCPError(-32602, f"Unknown tool: {tool_name}")
   309→    try:
   310→        result = await handler(arguments)
   311→        return {
   312→            "content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(result) if isinstance(result, dict) else str(result)}]
   313→        }
   314→    except SynapseError as e:
   315→        return {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": f"Error: {e.message}"}], "isError": True}
   316→```
   317→
   318→**CRITICAL:** `dispatch_tool` implements zero safety logic. It delegates to existing handlers which already enforce atomic scripts, idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions. The MCP layer is a thin protocol translation.

   396→#### Security
   397→
   398→- **Localhost binding only** by default (`127.0.0.1`, not `0.0.0.0`). Claude Code runs locally.

   413→## Testing Patterns
   414→
   415→**No Houdini required**: All tests import modules via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, bypassing the `hou` dependency. There is no shared `conftest.py` — each test file creates its own minimal `hou` stub inline via `sys.modules["hou"] = mock_hou`. Some test files (e.g., `test_guards.py`, `test_keyframe_aov.py`) save and restore the original `sys.modules["hou"]` in teardown to prevent cross-test pollution.
   416→
   417→**Patching `hou` in handler tests**: Always patch the module-level reference inside handlers.py, NOT `sys.modules["hou"]`. Patching sys.modules breaks object identity across test files.
   418→
   419→```python
   420→# Correct — patch the handlers module's hou reference
   421→_handlers_hou = handlers_mod.hou
   422→with patch.object(_handlers_hou, "node", return_value=mock_node):
   423→    ...
   424→
   425→# For attributes missing from the stub
   426→with patch.object(hou, "flipbook", create=True):
   427→    ...
   428→```
   429→
   430→**test_guards.py ordering**: Replaces `sys.modules["hou"]` entirely — has save/restore teardown to prevent pollution. `test_render.py` captures `_handlers_hou = handlers_mod.hou` to patch the correct object.
   431→
   432→**Error assertions**: Use `"Couldn't find"` (not `"not found"`) — matches coaching tone convention.
   433→
   434→**Windows encoding**: Any test writing files with em-dashes or special chars must use `encoding="utf-8"` (cp1252 breaks).
   435→
   436→**MCP protocol tests**: Test the JSON-RPC router, session management, tool dispatch, and resource reading without Houdini. Mock the handler registry to return canned responses. Verify correct error codes, header handling (`Mcp-Session-Id`, `MCP-Protocol-Version`), and content-type negotiation. Follow the same stub pattern as existing tests.

   438→## Adding New Functionality
   439→
   440→### Adding a new MCP tool
   441→
   442→1. Add `CommandType` variant in `core/protocol.py`
   443→2. Add handler method `_handle_<name>` in the appropriate handler file (`handlers.py` for core, `handlers_render.py` for render/viewport/keyframe/validation, `handlers_tops.py` for TOPS/PDG, `handlers_cops.py` for COPs/Copernicus, `handlers_material.py` for materials, `handlers_usd.py` for USD, `handlers_memory.py` for memory, `handlers_node.py` for node ops) and register it in `SynapseHandler._register_handlers()`
   444→3. Add parameter aliases in `core/aliases.py` if the tool has new parameter names
   445→4. Add `Tool(...)` entry to `list_tools()` and dispatch case to `call_tool()` in `mcp_server.py` (uses `Server.list_tools()`/`Server.call_tool()` decorators, not `@mcp.tool()` decorator pattern). All 107 tools defined in one `list_tools()` function with a single `call_tool()` switch
   446→5. **Add MCP tool definition in `mcp/tools.py`** — include `inputSchema` (JSON Schema for arguments) and `annotations` (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`). The tool dispatches to the same handler registered in step 2.
   447→6. Add timeout override to `_SLOW_COMMANDS` in `mcp_server.py` if >10s expected
   448→7. Write tests — bootstrap a `hou` stub inline via `sys.modules`, import handlers via `importlib`, patch `_handlers_hou` (not `sys.modules["hou"]`). **Also write a test in `test_mcp_protocol.py`** verifying the tool appears in `tools/list` and `tools/call` dispatches correctly.
   449→
   450→**Going forward, steps 5 and 7 (MCP registration + MCP test) are mandatory for all new tools.** The MCP tool registry is now the standard way to expose SYNAPSE functionality to external clients.

   453→
   454→Add to `routing/recipes.py` in the `_register_builtins()` method. 57 recipes. Recipes are Tier 0.5 — pattern-matched before regex, return multi-step command sequences. For complex workflows, use `execute_python` steps. For dynamic composition with modifiers ("set up X with Y and Z"), add workflow templates to `routing/planner.py`.

   456→### Adding RAG knowledge
   457→
   458→Add/edit files in `rag/skills/houdini21-reference/*.md` (78 files). Update topic triggers in `rag/documentation/_metadata/semantic_index.json` (28 topics, 400+ triggers).

   460→## Key Conventions
   461→
   462→**Coaching tone**: Error messages say "Couldn't find node" not "Node not found". Always offer next step. `_suggest_parms(node, name)` provides substring-matched alternatives. See `TONE.md` for the full voice guide.
   463→
   464→**He2025 determinism**: `round_float()` for OUTPUT only — never internal timing. `sort_keys=True` in all JSON serialization (both stdlib `json.dumps` and `orjson.OPT_SORT_KEYS`). `@deterministic` decorator auto-rounds float args. `kahan_sum()` for stable aggregation. Content-based UUIDs via `deterministic_uuid()`. Epoch-based adaptation uses fixed epoch SIZE (not time-based) per He2025.
   465→
   466→**Lazy loading**: `__init__.py` uses `__getattr__` to defer routing/server/UI imports. Optional deps use try/except with `*_AVAILABLE` flags. Keeps Houdini startup fast.
   467→
   468→**Thread safety**: `ReadWriteLock` (writer-priority) in `MemoryStore`. `threading.Lock()` for tier-pin cache. `threading.Event()` for background store loading. `_log_executor` ThreadPoolExecutor(2) for fire-and-forget memory logging.
   469→
   470→**Backwards compat**: All legacy names preserved — `NexusServer`, `EngramMemory`, `HyphaeAuditLog`, etc. Storage auto-migrates from `.nexus/`/`.engram/` to `.synapse/`.
   471→
   472→**Singletons**: `AuditLog`, `HumanGate`, `SynapseBridge`, `CryptoEngine` — accessed via `audit_log()`, `human_gate()`, `get_bridge()`, `get_crypto()`.
   473→
   474→**Error classification**: User errors (`ValueError`, `KeyError`, `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, `IndexError`, `NameError`) do NOT trip circuit breaker. Service errors (`TimeoutError`, threading errors, Houdini crashes) DO trip it.
   475→
   476→**Rollback errors in execute_python**: `_ROLLBACK_ERRORS = (NameError, SyntaxError, TypeError, AttributeError, IndexError)` trigger auto-undo. Operational errors (RuntimeError, hou.OperationFailed) do NOT — earlier mutations may be valid.
   477→
   478→## Lighting Law (Critical Domain Knowledge)
   479→
   480→**Intensity is ALWAYS 1.0 (or below)**. Brightness is controlled by **exposure** (logarithmic, in stops). This applies to ALL PBR renderers (Karma, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray).
   481→
   482→- Key:fill ratio 3:1 = 1.585 stops difference (`log2(3)`)
   483→- Key:fill ratio 4:1 = 2.0 stops difference (`log2(4)`)
   484→- USD exposure parm: `xn__inputsexposure_vya` (value), `xn__inputsexposure_control_wcb` = `"set"` (enable)
   485→- USD intensity parm: `xn__inputsintensity_i0a` — always 1.0
   486→
   487→## Rendering Guidelines
   488→
   489→When building or rendering Solaris scenes via MCP, follow a progressive validation pipeline — never jump straight to production settings:
   490→
   491→1. **Validate stage first**: After creating geometry, lights, and materials, query the stage to confirm all expected prims exist at correct paths. Use exact prim paths for material assignments (not wildcard patterns like `/**` unless verified).
   492→2. **Test render at low quality**: Start with 256x256 resolution, low pixel samples (4-8), no SSS, no displacement, no denoiser. Confirm the render completes and produces output before scaling up.
   493→3. **Scale incrementally**: Increase resolution and samples in steps. Enable expensive features (SSS, subsurface scattering, denoiser) one at a time.
   494→4. **Never use foreground rendering for heavy scenes**: `soho_foreground=1` blocks Houdini entirely — if the render is slow, the WebSocket server becomes unresponsive and the user must force-kill Houdini.
   495→5. **Verify output paths**: Set `picture` on the Karma LOP AND `outputimage` on the ROP. Check the output directory exists. Use `iconvert.exe` from `$HFS/bin/` for EXR-to-JPEG conversion.
   496→
   497→## Wire Protocol
   498→
   499→Default: `ws://localhost:9999/synapse` | Version: `4.0.0`
   500→MCP endpoint: `http://localhost:PORT/mcp` | Protocol: MCP 2025-06-18 (Streamable HTTP)
   501→
   502→106 registered handlers across 9 handler files:
   503→- **Core (23)**: `ping`, `get_health`, `get_help`, `create_node`, `delete_node`, `connect_nodes`, `get_parm`, `set_parm`, `get_scene_info`, `get_selection`, `execute_python`, `execute_vex`, `batch_commands`, `get_metrics`, `router_stats`, `list_recipes`, `knowledge_lookup`, `capture_viewport`, `undo`, `redo`, `network_explain`, `route_chat`, `project_setup`
   504→- **Render (11)**: `render`, `set_keyframe`, `render_settings`, `validate_frame`, `render_sequence`, `render_farm_status`, `solaris_validate_ordering`, `safe_render`, `render_progressively`, `autonomous_render`, `configure_render_passes`
   505→- **TOPS/PDG (20)**: `wedge`, `tops_get_work_items`, `tops_get_dependency_graph`, `tops_get_cook_stats`, `tops_cook_node`, `tops_generate_items`, `tops_configure_scheduler`, `tops_cancel_cook`, `tops_pause_cook`, `tops_resume_cook`, `tops_dirty_node`, `tops_setup_wedge`, `tops_batch_cook`, `tops_query_items`, `tops_cook_and_validate`, `tops_diagnose`, `tops_pipeline_status`, `tops_monitor_stream`, `tops_render_sequence`, `tops_multi_shot`
   506→- **COPs/Copernicus (20)**: `cops_create_network`, `cops_create_node`, `cops_connect`, `cops_set_opencl`, `cops_read_layer_info`, `cops_to_materialx`, `cops_composite_aovs`, `cops_analyze_render`, `cops_slap_comp`, `cops_create_solver`, `cops_procedural_texture`, `cops_growth_propagation`, `cops_reaction_diffusion`, `cops_pixel_sort`, `cops_stylize`, `cops_wetmap`, `cops_bake_textures`, `cops_temporal_analysis`, `cops_stamp_scatter`, `cops_batch_cook`
   507→- **HDA (5)**: `hda_create`, `hda_promote_parm`, `hda_set_help`, `hda_package`, `hda_list`
   508→- **Materials (4)**: `create_material`, `create_textured_material`, `assign_material`, `read_material`
   509→- **USD (10)**: `get_stage_info`, `get_usd_attribute`, `set_usd_attribute`, `create_usd_prim`, `modify_usd_prim`, `reference_usd`, `query_prims`, `manage_variant_set`, `manage_collection`, `configure_light_linking`
   510→- **Memory (13)**: `context`, `search`, `add_memory`, `decide`, `recall`, `inspect_selection`, `inspect_scene`, `inspect_node`, `memory_query`, `memory_status`, `memory_write`, `evolve_memory`, `get_live_metrics`
   511→
   512→All handlers are accessible through WebSocket, stdio MCP, and Streamable HTTP MCP transports. Parameter names resolve through `aliases.py` (38+ mappings) — e.g., `node`, `path`, `node_path` all resolve to canonical `node`.
   513→
   514→## Storage Layout
   515→
   516→```
   517→$HIP/.synapse/           # Per-project memory
   518→  memory.jsonl           # Append-only log (async write buffer: 2s flush / 50-item cap / atexit flush)
   519→  index.json             # Search indices (by_type, by_tag, by_keyword)
   520→  context.md             # Human-editable shot context
   521→  decisions.md           # Decision log
   522→  tasks.md               # Task history
   523→
   524→~/.synapse/              # Global
   525→  audit/                 # Daily JSONL audit logs (hash-chain, tamper-evident)
   526→  gates/                 # Gate proposals (timestamped, immutable)
   527→  encryption.key         # Auto-generated Fernet key (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256)
   528→  agent/                 # Autonomous agent SDK (synapse_agent.py entry point)
   529→  design/                # Design tokens, icon generator, Qt styles
   530→  houdini/               # Shelf, panel, callbacks for Houdini integration
   531→  install.py             # Houdini prefs installer
   532→```
   533→
   534→## Gotchas
   535→
   536→- **matlib.cook(force=True)**: MUST cook materiallibrary before `createNode()` on shader child — without cook, internal subnet doesn't exist and createNode returns None
   537→- **Render output_file kwarg**: Doesn't work for usdrender ROPs — set `outputimage` or `picture` parm directly
   538→- **usdrender loppath**: ROPs in `/out` need `loppath` set to a LOP node — handler auto-discovers display node in `/stage`
   539→- **Karma camera**: Must use USD prim path (`/cameras/render_cam`), not Houdini node path
   540→- **override_res**: String menu `""` / `"scale"` / `"specific"` — not int
   541→- **Viewport capture**: Must use Flipbook API with `hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResult()` — `QWidget.grab()` returns black for OpenGL; `executeDeferred()` is fire-and-forget and won't block
   542→- **.pypanel imports**: NEVER nuke `sys.modules` — use `hou.session` guard for one-time import
   543→- **RAG Path import**: Handler uses `from pathlib import Path as _Path` (inline) — global `Path` not available in handlers.py
   544→- **MCP execute_python**: MCP param is `code`, but Synapse handler resolves `content` — payload builder in mcp_server.py maps it
   545→- **SVG icon generation**: XML forbids `--` inside comments; use `|` separator
   546→- **synapse_shelf.py**: Security hooks block `parm.eval()` patterns; use `node.evalParm("parm_name")` method instead
   547→- **Agent SDK websockets**: Must import at module level (not inside connect()) — patch target is `synapse_ws.websockets`
   548→- **Zombie servers**: Multiple SynapseServer instances can linger in Houdini; use `gc.get_objects()` + `_actual_port` to find the active one
   549→- **MCP tool registration (stdio bridge)**: Uses `@server.list_tools()` returning `Tool(...)` list + `@server.call_tool()` dispatcher — NOT the `@mcp.tool()` decorator pattern. All 107 tools defined in one `list_tools()` function with a single `call_tool()` switch
   550→- **MCP tool registration (Streamable HTTP)**: Uses the tool registry in `mcp/tools.py` which maps to the same handlers. Both registries must stay in sync — when adding a tool to `mcp_server.py`, also add it to `mcp/tools.py`
   551→- **MCP session headers**: `Mcp-Session-Id` must be returned on the `initialize` response and included by the client on all subsequent requests. hwebserver header access may require case-insensitive lookup
   552→- **MCP notifications return 202**: `notifications/initialized` and other notification methods return HTTP 202 Accepted with empty body — NOT 200 with a JSON-RPC response
   553→- **MCP protocol version header**: Clients may send `MCP-Protocol-Version` header. If present and unsupported, respond with 400 Bad Request per spec
   554→- **SYNAPSE_PATH env var**: Controls WebSocket path segment (default `/synapse`). `SYNAPSE_PORT` controls port (default `9999`). Full URL: `ws://localhost:{SYNAPSE_PORT}{SYNAPSE_PATH}`
   555→- **orjson optional**: `protocol.py` and `mcp_server.py` use `orjson` for fast JSON with `OPT_SORT_KEYS` when installed, auto-fallback to stdlib `json`

    53→
    54→## Cross-Project Architecture
    55→
    56→These projects form an interconnected ecosystem, not isolated tools. Understanding the relationships prevents duplicate work and wrong-target edits.
    57→
    58→### Project Dependency Graph
    59→
    60→```
    61→Orchestra (cognitive safety)
    62→  |-- provides: PRISM signal detection, MoE expert routing, BCM learning trails
    63→  |-- consumed by: Synapse (coaching tone adaptation), OTTO (constitutional gating)
    64→
    65→Synapse (Houdini AI exoskeleton)
    66→  |-- provides: 43 MCP tools, 6-tier routing, USD-native memory, render validation
    67→  |-- depends on: Houdini Python API (hou module), WebSocket transport

    70→
    71→comfyui-agent (ComfyUI AI assistant)
    72→  |-- provides: 61 tools (understand/discover/pilot/verify), vision module, memory
    73→  |-- parallel to Synapse — same exoskeleton pattern, different DCC app
    74→
    75→Optimizer (workstation tuning)
    76→  |-- provides: NVML telemetry, Houdini memory/OCL settings, GPU power management
    77→  |-- feeds into: Synapse pre-render checks, ComfyUI VRAM awareness
    78→
    79→vex-corpus (VEX training data)
    80→  |-- provides: labeled VEX examples with difficulty ratings, consensus validation
    81→  |-- feeds into: Synapse RAG knowledge layer
    82→```
    83→
    84→### Shared Architectural Patterns
    85→
    86→Every major project implements these patterns. When modifying one project, check if the pattern exists in sibling projects:
    87→
    88→- **Memory with temporal decay** — Orchestra: 2h half-life BCM trails. OTTO: 168h half-life outcome trails. comfyui-agent: 7-day half-life. Synapse: JSONL/SQLite with Charmander->Charmeleon->Charizard evolution.
    89→- **MCP integration** — Synapse: 107 MCP tools via stdio + Streamable HTTP. comfyui-agent: 65 tools via MCP adapter. Orchestra: orchestra-mcp package. All expose tools following the same handler pattern.
    90→- **Resilience stack** — Circuit breakers, rate limiters, health checks. Synapse and comfyui-agent both implement this. Don't reinvent — follow the existing `resilience.py` pattern.
    91→- **Human-in-the-loop gates** — INFORM/REVIEW/APPROVE/CRITICAL levels. Synapse and RadiantSuite share this pattern via `GateProposal`.
    92→- **Coaching tone** — Synapse and OTTO both use "collaborative senior colleague" voice. Errors are "we hit a snag" not "invalid input."
    93→
    94→## Cross-Project Patterns
    95→
    96→### Determinism Requirements
    97→
    98→All major projects enforce application-level determinism (same inputs = same outputs):
    99→- `sort_keys=True` in all JSON serialization
   100→- Sorted dict iterations before aggregation
   101→- Stable tiebreakers (no `uuid.uuid4()` in hot paths, use deterministic IDs)
   102→- `time.time()` not used in seeds or hashing
   103→
   104→Inspired by the batch-invariance *principle* from ThinkingMachines (Horace He, 2025), which shows that individual GPU kernels are run-to-run deterministic but system-level nondeterminism arises from batch-size variance changing reduction order. Orchestra additionally implements kernel-level patterns: `COGNITIVE_TILE_SIZE=32` + Kahan summation for numerically stable aggregation.
   105→
   106→### Python Version
   107→
   108→**Python 3.14** is the system default. Key breaking change: `asyncio.get_event_loop()` raises `RuntimeError` outside a running loop. Use `@pytest.mark.asyncio` or `asyncio.run()` instead.
   109→
   110→### Testing
   111→
   112→- All Python projects use **pytest** (no unittest)
   113→- Orchestra uses `pytest.ini` (not pyproject.toml for pytest config); has `asyncio_mode=auto`
   114→- `--timeout` flag unavailable (pytest-timeout not installed)
   115→- Orchestra CI excludes: `test_integration.py`, `test_performance.py`, `test_chaos.py`
   116→
   117→### Installation Pattern
   118→
   119→All major projects: `pip install -e ".[dev]"` for development. Optional features via extras (e.g., `".[dev,websocket,mcp]"`).
   120→
   121→### Running a Single Test
   122→
   123→```bash
   124→# Single test file
   125→python -m pytest tests/test_routing.py -v
   126→
   127→# Single test function
   128→python -m pytest tests/test_routing.py::test_cache_hit -v
   129→
   130→# Tests matching a keyword
   131→python -m pytest tests/ -v -k "recipe"
   132→
   133→# Orchestra (from project root, uses pytest.ini)
   134→cd Orchestra && python -m pytest tests/test_nexus.py::TestNexusPipeline::test_phase_ordering -v
   135→```
   136→
   137→### Windows Environment
   138→
   139→This is a Windows 11 development environment. Always account for platform-specific behavior:
   140→
   141→- **Shell selection**: Use **PowerShell** (not cmd or Git Bash) for: environment variables (`setx`), registry edits (`reg add`), elevated commands, and path-sensitive operations. Git Bash silently mangles `setx` escaping and swallows UAC interactions.
   142→- **UAC elevation**: Inline `Start-Process -Verb RunAs` often fails due to prompt timing. For elevated commands, **write a temp .ps1 script and invoke it** instead of piping inline commands.
   143→- **Encoding**: Default is cp1252, not UTF-8. Use ASCII arrows (`<-`) not Unicode. All Python `open()` calls need explicit `encoding='utf-8'`.
   144→- **App Execution Aliases**: Windows ships zero-byte stubs in `WindowsApps/` that shadow real binaries. When a CLI tool fails mysteriously, check `where <tool>` and `Get-Command <tool>` in PowerShell.
   145→- **Imports for mocking**: `httpx`, `websockets` must be module-level for `mock.patch` to work.
   146→- **Platform**: AMD Threadripper PRO 7965WX (24C/48T), RTX 4090 (24GB), 128GB DDR5.
   147→
   148→### Source vs Deployed — Edit the Right Files
   149→
   150→**CRITICAL: Always edit repo source files, never deployed or installed copies.**
   151→
   152→Before editing any file, confirm it is in the repository source tree. If you're unsure which copy is canonical, ask.
   153→
   154→| Repo Source (EDIT THIS) | Deployed Copy (NEVER EDIT) |
   155→|---|---|
   156→| `Synapse/` | `~/.synapse/houdini/`, `~/.synapse/agent/`, `~/.synapse/design/` |
   157→| `Orchestra/` | `~/.orchestra/` |
   158→| `comfyui-agent/` | Any installed site-packages copy |
   159→| `~/.claude/commands/` | N/A (these ARE the source) |
   160→| `~/.claude/skills/` | N/A (these ARE the source) |
   161→
   162→If a path contains `node_modules/`, `site-packages/`, `dist/`, `.synapse/`, or `.orchestra/` — it is a deployed copy. Do not edit it.
   163→
   164→### Process Awareness
   165→
   166→Before starting long-running pipelines, renders, or background scripts:
   167→
   168→1. **Check if a previous instance is still running** — use `Get-Process` (PowerShell) or `tasklist` (cmd) to verify.
   169→2. **Never start a duplicate process** without confirming the old one is dead.
   170→3. **For Houdini**: Check if `houdini.exe` or `hbatch.exe` is already running before launching new instances.
   171→
   172→### Validate Before Scaling Up
   173→
   174→Before running any render or system-level command, first do a minimal dry-run version:
   175→- **Renders**: Use 320x240, no displacement, no SSS. Confirm output before increasing quality.
   176→- **Environment changes** (`setx`, registry): Echo the command and verify syntax before executing.
   177→- **Elevated commands**: Test in a non-elevated subprocess first when possible.
   178→
   179→### Language & Style
   180→
   181→- **Primary language**: Python. All major projects (Orchestra, Synapse, OTTO, comfyui-agent) are Python.
   182→- **Secondary**: TypeScript/React (jaimeibrahim.com portfolio site)
   183→- **Determinism compliance** is required for all Houdini-related and AI framework code (see Determinism Requirements above)
   184→- **Coaching tone** for Synapse error messages (see project CLAUDE.md)
   185→
   186→## Shared Infrastructure

   189→
   190→- `CLAUDE.md` — Cognitive substrate: reasoning protocols, workflow scaffolds, code patterns (always auto-loaded)
   191→- `commands/` — 16 slash-command agents from [Context-Engineering](https://github.com/davidkimai/Context-Engineering) (`/research`, `/test`, `/security`, `/optimize`, `/deploy`, `/monitor`, `/cli`, `/doc`, `/data`, `/meta`, `/alignment`, `/diligence`, `/legal`, `/lit`, `/marketing`, `/comms`)
   192→- `substrate/tools/` — Substrate tool suite (293 tests, 86% coverage)
   193→- `substrate/knowledge/` — Knowledge prims (89 prims, 340+ triggers)
   194→- `projects/_index.md` — Project orchestration (FOCUS/HOLDING/PARKED status)

   197→### `~/.synapse/` — Synapse Companion

   200→- `design/` — Complete design system (tokens, 21 SVGs, Qt styles)
   201→- `houdini/` — Shelf and panel integration for Houdini
   202→- `install.py` — Installer with `--dry-run`, `--verify`, `--uninstall`

   206→- `bcm/` — BCM learning trails (2-hour decay half-life)
   207→- `state/` — Session state
   208→
   209→## Lighting Law (VFX — Never Violate)
   210→
   211→When working with any PBR renderer (Karma, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray):
   212→- **Intensity is ALWAYS 1.0 or below** — never set intensity > 1
   213→- **Brightness controlled by EXPOSURE** (logarithmic, in stops)
   214→- Key:fill ratio 3:1 = 1.585 stops difference; 4:1 = 2.0 stops

1→"""
     2→Canonical Tool Registry -- Single Source of Truth
     3→
     4→Every MCP tool definition lives here. Both transports import from this module:
     5→- stdio bridge (mcp_server.py) generates Tool() objects from TOOL_DEFS
     6→- Streamable HTTP (mcp/tools.py) builds JSON tool definitions from TOOL_DEFS
     7→
     8→Adding a new tool:
     9→1. Add handler in the appropriate handlers_*.py file
    10→2. Add entry to TOOL_DEFS in this file
    11→3. Both transports pick it up automatically
    12→
    13→No hou dependency. No imports from synapse.server or synapse.mcp.tools.
    14→Only json and orjson (optional).
    15→"""
    16→
    17→import json
    18→from typing import Any
    19→
    20→try:
    21→    import orjson
    22→
    23→    def _dumps_str(obj) -> str:
    24→        return orjson.dumps(obj, option=orjson.OPT_SORT_KEYS).decode()
    25→except ImportError:
    26→
    27→    def _dumps_str(obj) -> str:
    28→        return json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True)
    29→
    30→
    31→# =========================================================================
    32→# Dispatch ID counter (He2025: sequential, not uuid4)
    33→# =========================================================================
    34→
    35→_call_counter = 0
    36→
    37→
    38→def _next_call_id(tool_name: str) -> str:
    39→    global _call_counter
    40→    _call_counter += 1
    41→    return f"mcp-{tool_name}-{_call_counter}"
    42→
    43→
    44→# =========================================================================
    45→# Payload builders (transform MCP arguments to handler payload)
    46→# =========================================================================
    47→
    48→
    49→def _passthrough(_args: dict) -> dict:
    50→    return {}
    51→
    52→
    53→def _identity(args: dict) -> dict:
    54→    return dict(args)
    55→
    56→
    57→def _execute_python_payload(args: dict) -> dict:
    58→    p = {"content": args["code"]}
    59→    if "dry_run" in args:
    60→        p["dry_run"] = args["dry_run"]
    61→    if "atomic" in args:
    62→        p["atomic"] = args["atomic"]
    63→    return p
    64→
    65→
    66→def _stage_info_payload(args: dict) -> dict:
    67→    p = {}
    68→    if "node" in args:
    69→        p["node"] = args["node"]
    70→    return p
    71→
    72→
    73→def _decide_payload(args: dict) -> dict:
    74→    p = {"decision": args["decision"]}
    75→    if "reasoning" in args:
    76→        p["reasoning"] = args["reasoning"]
    77→    if "alternatives" in args:
    78→        alt = args["alternatives"]
    79→        p["alternatives"] = (
    80→            [a.strip() for a in alt.split(",") if a.strip()]
    81→            if isinstance(alt, str) else alt
    82→        )
    83→    return p
    84→
    85→
    86→def _add_memory_payload(args: dict) -> dict:
    87→    p = {"content": args["content"]}
    88→    if "memory_type" in args:
    89→        p["memory_type"] = args["memory_type"]
    90→    if "tags" in args:
    91→        p["tags"] = args["tags"]
    92→    return p
    93→
    94→
    95→def _filter_keys(keys):
    96→    """Return a payload builder that passes through only the specified keys."""
    97→    def _builder(args: dict) -> dict:
    98→        return {k: args[k] for k in keys if k in args}
    99→    return _builder
